concepts.subsection: Weighted average cost of capital
concepts.statement: WACC weights each source of finance by its market value, not its book value, and uses debt's after-tax cost, not its quoted rate — the tax shield on interest is part of what debt actually costs the firm. Book-value weights or a pre-tax cost of debt both misstate the discount rate applied to project cash flows.

concepts.subsection: Advanced Capital Budgeting Decisions — real options
concepts.statement: A project's strategic value is its static NPV plus the value of the flexibility attached to it — options to expand, abandon or delay that ordinary discounting prices at zero. A negative static NPV can still be worth taking up when the option it carries is worth more than the shortfall.

concepts.subsection: Risk in capital budgeting — sensitivity, scenario and simulation
concepts.statement: Sensitivity analysis moves one variable at a time to find each one's break-even point. Scenario analysis moves several variables together in a few named, internally consistent bundles — best, base, worst. Simulation draws thousands of random combinations from each variable's probability distribution and builds the full outcome distribution, which the other two only sample at a handful of points.

concepts.subsection: Derivatives Analysis and Valuation
concepts.statement: A one-step binomial model prices an option from the two possible next-period stock prices using the risk-neutral probability that makes the stock's own expected return equal the risk-free rate — not the real-world probability of an up move, which plays no part in a no-arbitrage price. The expected payoff under that probability is then discounted at the risk-free rate.

concepts.subsection: Derivatives Analysis and Valuation — Black-Scholes inputs
concepts.statement: Black-Scholes prices an option from five inputs: spot, strike, time to expiry, the risk-free rate and volatility. A call rises with spot, time, the rate and volatility, and falls with a higher strike; volatility raises both the call and the put together, since either option gains from a larger move and loses no more than its premium either way.

concepts.subsection: Security Valuation — convexity
concepts.statement: Duration prices the bond's yield sensitivity as a straight line; convexity is the curvature that line misses. Because the true price-yield curve bends away from the line, a positive-convexity bond gains more from a yield fall than duration predicts and loses less from an equal yield rise — the convexity term always adds back value that a duration-only estimate leaves out.

concepts.subsection: Security Valuation — yield measures
concepts.statement: Current yield is the annual coupon divided by the bond's market price, not its face value. For a bond trading below par, the order runs coupon rate < current yield < yield to maturity, because YTM also captures the pull to par at redemption that current yield ignores; above par the order reverses, and only a par bond has all three equal.

concepts.subsection: Risk Management — credit default swaps
concepts.statement: A credit default swap transfers a bond's default risk from a protection buyer to a protection seller: the buyer pays a periodic spread regardless of what happens, and the seller pays out only if the reference entity defaults, and then only the loss given default — the face value less whatever the recovery rate returns.

concepts.subsection: Rights issue — theoretical ex-rights price
concepts.statement: The theoretical ex-rights price weights the cum-rights price and the subscription price by the number of old and new shares, not by a simple average of the two prices. The value of the right attached to one existing share is the ex-rights price less the subscription price, divided by the number of old shares needed to subscribe for one new share.

concepts.subsection: Dividend policy — Walter's model
concepts.statement: Walter's model prices a share as P = [D + (r/Ke)(E − D)] / Ke and ties the optimal payout to how the firm's internal return r compares with its cost of equity Ke — retain everything when r exceeds Ke, since the firm compounds cash better than the market prices it; pay out everything when r is below Ke; payout is irrelevant only at r = Ke, the special case MM's irrelevance proposition generalises.

concepts.subsection: Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring — leveraged buyouts
concepts.statement: A leveraged buyout funds most of the purchase price with debt secured on the target's own assets and cash flows, leaving the sponsor's equity a small slice of the deal. Returns come from paying that debt down over the holding period — and from any exit-multiple expansion — so the same flat operating performance produces a far larger percentage return on the sponsor's equity than on the deal as a whole.

citation.ref: Ch. Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

concepts.subsection: Portfolio Management — two-asset risk and correlation
concepts.statement: A two-asset portfolio's standard deviation equals the weighted average of the two assets' standard deviations only when they are perfectly positively correlated. At any lower correlation the covariance term in the variance formula is smaller than that limiting case, and the portfolio's risk falls below the weighted average — the diversification benefit correlation below one always buys.

concepts.subsection: Advanced Capital Budgeting Decisions — unequal lives and equivalent annual cost
concepts.statement: Two assets that do the same job over different lives cannot be compared on total present value of cost, because the shorter-lived one simply carries fewer years of cost. Each total is converted into an equivalent annual cost by dividing it by the annuity factor for its own life — not by the number of years, which would throw away the time value the annuity factor holds — and the lower annual charge wins.

concepts.subsection: Advanced Capital Budgeting Decisions — adjusted present value
concepts.statement: APV splits a project in two rather than folding financing into the discount rate: value it first as if it were all-equity funded, at the ungeared cost of equity, then add every financing side effect separately — the present value of the interest tax shield, less issue costs, plus any subsidised-loan benefit. The tax shield is the tax saved on the interest, not the interest itself, and a project can turn from reject to accept on the financing half alone.

concepts.subsection: Business Valuation — enterprise multiples and the bridge to equity value
concepts.statement: An EV/EBITDA multiple prices the whole enterprise, so what it produces belongs to lenders and shareholders together. Getting from there to a share price means walking the bridge — deduct the debt, add back the cash the buyer also acquires, then divide by shares outstanding. Deducting gross debt without crediting the cash, or skipping the bridge entirely, values the equity at the whole firm's worth.

concepts.subsection: Foreign exchange — purchasing power parity and expected spot rates
concepts.statement: Relative purchasing power parity says the expected spot rate moves with the ratio of the two countries' expected inflation, so the higher-inflation currency is expected to depreciate. Quoting home currency per unit of foreign currency, the expected rate is the spot multiplied by one plus home inflation over one plus foreign inflation. Where interest rate parity works from interest rates and binds today's forward, PPP works from inflation and predicts a future spot.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.subsection: Foreign exchange — multilateral netting, leading and lagging
concepts.statement: Multilateral netting collapses every intra-group payable and receivable into one net position per company through a central desk, so only the net balances actually cross a border and only those bear conversion and transfer cost. It beats bilateral netting, which settles each pair on its own and leaves flows that would have cancelled group-wide. Leading and lagging is the companion timing tool — settle early in a currency expected to strengthen, delay in one expected to weaken.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.subsection: Derivatives Analysis and Valuation — delta and the hedge ratio
concepts.statement: Delta is how much an option's value moves for a one-rupee move in the underlying — between zero and one for a call, between minus one and zero for a put — and it doubles as the hedge ratio. A written call position is neutralised by holding delta times the number of underlying shares the options cover. The hedge holds only locally, because delta itself shifts as the share moves, which is why a delta hedge must be rebalanced rather than set once.

concepts.subsection: Interest Rate Risk Management — swaptions
concepts.statement: A swaption is an option on a swap, not on a rate. A payer swaption gives its buyer the right, never the obligation, to enter a swap as the fixed-rate payer, so it protects a borrower against rates rising while leaving the gain if rates fall; a receiver swaption is the mirror, the right to receive fixed, which suits a lender or an investor fearing a fall. The buyer pays a premium and holds the right; the writer collects the premium and carries the obligation.

concepts.subsection: Portfolio Management — rebalancing strategies and portfolio insurance
concepts.statement: The three rebalancing disciplines pull in different directions after a market move. Buy-and-hold does nothing. Constant mix restores a fixed percentage split, so it buys into a fall and sells into a rise. Constant proportion portfolio insurance sets the equity holding at a multiplier times the cushion — portfolio value less the floor — so a fall shrinks the cushion and forces selling, which is what keeps the floor intact.

concepts.subsection: Portfolio Management — Sharpe's single index model and the cut-off rate
concepts.statement: Sharpe's single index model builds the optimal portfolio by ranking securities on excess return to beta — expected return less the risk-free rate, divided by beta — and admitting every security whose ratio exceeds the computed cut-off rate. The ratio, not the raw expected return, decides: a high-return security carrying a heavy beta can rank below a modest one that earns its return cheaply, and the cut-off is a threshold that admits several securities, not a contest the top name wins alone.

concepts.subsection: Corporate restructuring — demerger, sell-off and equity carve-out
concepts.statement: The three ways of separating a division differ in who ends up owning it and whether cash comes in. A demerger or spin-off hands shares in the new company to the parent's own shareholders in proportion to their holding — no buyer, no consideration, no cash. A sell-off sells the division outright to a third party for cash. An equity carve-out floats a minority stake in the subsidiary to outside investors, raising cash while the parent keeps control.

citation.ref: Ch. Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

concepts.subsection: International Financial Management — depository receipts and cross-market pricing
concepts.statement: A depository receipt is issued abroad by an overseas depository against a fixed number of home-market shares held by a domestic custodian, and that ratio is what makes the two prices comparable. Convert the receipt's foreign currency price at spot and set it against the ratio times the home share price: a gap either way is a premium or a discount, and it is measured against the underlying shares' value, since that is what the receipt is a claim on.

concepts.subsection: Financial restructuring — share buyback and earnings per share
concepts.statement: A buyback funded from surplus cash cuts the share count, which lifts EPS, but it also surrenders the after-tax income that cash was earning, which lowers it. The net effect turns on which is larger, so the working must charge the earnings forgone net of tax — not gross — and divide by the reduced share count. Counting one side without the other guarantees the wrong answer, and in either direction.

citation.ref: Ch. Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

concepts.subsection: Security Valuation — callable bonds and yield to call
concepts.statement: A callable bond hands the issuer, not the investor, the right to redeem early at a stated call price. Yield to maturity therefore describes an outcome the investor may never see: for a bond trading above par the issuer can refinance more cheaply and will call. The honest number is the yield to worst — the lower of yield to maturity and yield to call — and the yield to call is worked on the call price and the call date, over the average of the purchase price and the call price.

concepts.subsection: Security Valuation — convertible debentures, conversion value and premium
concepts.statement: A convertible debenture has two values underneath it. Conversion value is the conversion ratio times the share price; straight bond value is what the same coupon and maturity would fetch without the conversion right. The floor is whichever of the two is higher, because the holder can always fall back on it. The conversion premium is the market price less the conversion value — measured from the price actually paid, not from face value, and expressed against the conversion value it exceeds.

concepts.subsection: Derivatives Analysis and Valuation — warrants and equity dilution
concepts.statement: A warrant is written by the company itself, which is what separates it from an exchange-traded call option written by another investor. Exercise brings the exercise price into the company in cash and makes it issue new shares, so the share count rises and existing holders dilute; an option merely moves existing shares between two outsiders. A detachable warrant is a security in its own right, separately listed and separately priced, and exercising it leaves the debenture it came attached to still outstanding — where a convertible debenture is extinguished on conversion.

concepts.subsection: Advanced Capital Budgeting Decisions — the abandonment option
concepts.statement: The option to abandon is exercised state by state, not once for the whole project: at the decision date, compare the abandonment value with the present value of continuing in that state and take the larger. Its worth is the expected gain over the states where abandoning wins, discounted back — never the raw abandonment proceeds, and never the gain in the worst state taken alone. A static NPV that discounts probability-weighted cash flows prices this flexibility at exactly zero, which is how a rejected project turns acceptable.

concepts.subsection: Leasing decisions — the lessor's break-even rental
concepts.statement: The lessor's break-even rental is the annual rental at which the present value of what he receives equals what the asset cost him. What he receives each year is the rental net of tax plus the depreciation tax shield he claims as owner — leaving the shield out asks the rental to recover money the taxman is already returning. Discounting at his required after-tax return through the annuity factor, and then grossing the answer back up by one minus the tax rate, gives the rental.

concepts.subsection: Leasing decisions — sale and leaseback
concepts.statement: A sale and leaseback is a financing transaction wearing a disposal's clothes. Cash equal to the sale price comes in, and a stream of committed rentals goes out — an obligation the owner did not have before. Because the rentals are priced off the sale price, a higher price simply buys a higher rental, so the accounting profit over book value measures nothing. The test is the implicit interest rate in the rentals against the cost of borrowing the same money, and the real costs are the depreciation shield and the residual value handed to the lessor.

concepts.subsection: Dividend policy — Lintner's model and dividend smoothing
concepts.statement: Lintner's model says the dividend moves only part of the way towards its target each year: the target dividend is the target payout ratio times current earnings, and this year's dividend is last year's plus the speed of adjustment times the gap between the two. The adjustment factor multiplies the gap, never the earnings. The smoothing exists because managers know a cut is punished far harder than a rise is rewarded, so they raise slowly and hold on the way down.

concepts.subsection: Dividend policy — the residual approach
concepts.statement: Under a residual dividend policy investment comes first and the dividend is what survives. The claim on earnings is only the equity portion of the capital budget — the target equity weight times the budget — because the rest is borrowed to hold the capital structure steady. Whatever profit is left after that is paid out, so the payout ratio moves year to year with the size of the capital budget, which is the opposite of a constant payout policy.

concepts.subsection: Currency swaps — comparative advantage and the quality spread differential
concepts.statement: The gain in a currency swap comes from comparative advantage, not absolute advantage. One party may borrow more cheaply than the other in both currencies and the swap still creates value, because what matters is that its edge is wider in one currency than in the other. Each borrows where its edge is widest and swaps into what it wants, and the total gain available — the quality spread differential — is the difference between the two spreads, never their sum.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.subsection: Portfolio Management — Fama's decomposition and net selectivity
concepts.statement: Fama splits a fund's return into what the risk taken required and what the manager added. Required return for systematic risk uses beta; required return for total risk uses the ratio of the fund's standard deviation to the market's. Gross selectivity is the return above the beta-based requirement — Jensen's alpha. Net selectivity subtracts the diversification cost, the gap between the two requirements, and so charges the manager for holding risk he did not have to hold. Only net selectivity is stock picking paid for in full.

concepts.subsection: International Financial Management — factoring and forfaiting
concepts.statement: Factoring buys short-term trade debts, usually as a continuing book rather than one deal, advances a part of each invoice, may be with or without recourse, and normally carries sales ledger administration and collection with it. Forfaiting discounts a single medium- to long-term export receivable evidenced by a negotiable instrument, usually avalised by the importer's bank, always without recourse to the exporter, at a fixed discount rate and with no ledger service. Recourse is the sharpest test between them.

concepts.subsection: International Financial Management — Islamic finance and Sukuk
concepts.statement: Islamic finance forbids riba — a guaranteed return on money lent — but not return itself: profit earned by owning an asset and carrying its risk is permitted. A Sukuk is therefore not a bond with the coupon renamed. Its holder takes beneficial ownership of an identified underlying asset and is paid from what that asset earns, whether rent under an Ijarah structure or a share of profit under Musharakah. Ownership and asset risk, not the name given to the payment, are what make the return permissible.

concepts.subsection: International Financial Management — country risk premium in the cost of equity
concepts.statement: A subsidiary in a developing country is not valued at a mature-market cost of equity. A country risk premium, commonly proxied by the sovereign yield spread over comparable home government paper, is added — and there are two ways of adding it. Carried through beta, it joins the equity risk premium before beta multiplies, so a business more exposed than average to its market is charged more than average for country risk. Added flat, every business in that country carries the same premium. The two differ, and the method has to be stated.

concepts.subsection: Derivatives Analysis and Valuation — commodity futures and basis risk
concepts.statement: A buyer of a commodity hedges by going long futures, so a rise in the price he must pay is met by a gain on the futures leg that reduces his effective cost. The hedge does not lock the entry futures price: it locks that price plus the basis — spot less futures — prevailing when the hedge is lifted. Because the closing basis is unknown today, basis risk survives the hedge, and it is the whole reason the effective cost lands near the futures price rather than on it.

concepts.subsection: Risk Management — what a credit rating says and does not say
concepts.statement: A credit rating is an opinion on the likelihood that one specific instrument is serviced on time — so the same company's long-term facilities and its commercial paper can be rated differently, since tenure, security and structure all move the grade. It is not investment advice: it ranks default risk and is deliberately silent on whether the price or yield on offer compensates for that risk. It is not permanent either; the agency keeps the issuer under surveillance and rating migration, including to default grade, is ordinary.

concepts.subsection: Business Valuation — financial distress prediction and the Z-score
concepts.statement: Altman's Z-score predicts corporate distress from a weighted sum of accounting ratios, and the weights are the model — an unweighted total of the same ratios is a different number that means nothing. Every ratio goes in, each at its own coefficient, and the market value term takes the market's own view rather than book equity. The verdict has three zones, not two: a safe zone, a distress zone, and a grey zone in between where the model declines to call it either way.

concepts.subsection: Portfolio Management
concepts.statement: Diversification removes unsystematic risk, the part specific to individual securities. What remains in a well-diversified portfolio is systematic risk, which beta measures and which no amount of diversification can remove.

concepts.subsection: Derivatives Analysis and Valuation
concepts.statement: An option premium is intrinsic value plus time value. A put's intrinsic value is the excess of strike over spot (zero if spot is higher); whatever of the premium is not intrinsic value is time value.

concepts.subsection: Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management
concepts.statement: Under interest rate parity, the currency with the higher interest rate trades at a forward discount and the lower-rate currency at a forward premium, by the interest differential — otherwise borrowing in one currency and depositing in the other would be a free profit.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.subsection: Security Valuation
concepts.statement: Duration measures a bond's price sensitivity to interest rate changes. It rises with maturity and falls with coupon; a zero-coupon bond's duration equals its maturity, the maximum for any bond of that term.

concepts.subsection: Derivatives Analysis and Valuation
concepts.statement: To hedge a stock portfolio with index futures, the number of contracts is the portfolio's value multiplied by its beta, divided by the value of one futures contract. Ignoring beta hedges a different portfolio than the one held.

concepts.subsection: Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management
concepts.statement: An importer with a foreign currency payable loses when that currency rises, so the hedge is to buy it forward or buy a call option on it. A forward locks the rate both ways; the option caps the cost while keeping the gain if the currency falls, at the price of the premium.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.subsection: Advanced Capital Budgeting Decisions
concepts.statement: When mutually exclusive projects rank differently under NPV and IRR, NPV decides. IRR assumes reinvestment at the IRR itself and can prefer a small project with a high rate over a large one that adds more value; NPV measures the wealth actually added at the real cost of capital.

concepts.subsection: Mutual Funds
concepts.statement: Net asset value per unit is the market value of the fund's investments plus other assets, minus liabilities and accrued expenses, divided by units outstanding. Entry and exit prices derive from NAV, and the expense ratio quietly drags it every day.

concepts.subsection: Business Valuation
concepts.statement: Under constant dividend growth, equity value per share is next year's expected dividend divided by the excess of the required return over the growth rate. The model runs on the coming dividend, not the one just paid, and dies where growth meets or beats the required return.

concepts.subsection: Interest Rate Risk Management
concepts.statement: A forward rate agreement fixes today the interest rate for a future borrowing or deposit period — a 6x9 FRA covers a three-month period starting six months out. The buyer gains when rates rise above the agreed rate and is compensated by a discounted settlement at the period's start; no principal ever moves.

concepts.subsection: Derivatives Analysis and Valuation
concepts.statement: For European options on the same share, strike and expiry, the call price minus the put price equals the share price minus the present value of the strike. When market prices break that chain, a riskless arbitrage exists — buy the cheap side, sell the dear one, and lock the difference.

concepts.subsection: Portfolio performance measures
concepts.statement: Sharpe divides excess return by total risk (standard deviation); Treynor divides the same excess return by systematic risk (beta). For a fully diversified portfolio the two rank alike, because diversification has squeezed out the unsystematic part. Where they disagree, the fund is carrying diversifiable risk the market does not pay for.

concepts.subsection: CAPM and the security market line
concepts.statement: CAPM's required return is the risk-free rate plus beta times the market risk premium. A security whose expected return sits above that line has positive alpha — it is underpriced, and the decision rule says buy; below the line, overpriced, sell. Alpha measures mispricing against systematic risk only.

concepts.subsection: Futures pricing — cost of carry
concepts.statement: The fair futures price is the spot price grown at the carrying cost — financing, storage, minus any yield the asset throws off. A traded futures price above fair value invites cash-and-carry arbitrage (buy spot, sell futures); below fair value, reverse cash-and-carry (sell spot, buy futures). The arbitrage, not opinion, is what pins the price to the formula.

concepts.subsection: Mergers — exchange ratio and EPS
concepts.statement: In a share-for-share merger, the acquirer's EPS rises when the price paid values the target at a lower price-earnings multiple than the acquirer's own, and falls when the target is bought at a higher multiple. The exchange ratio decides how the combined earnings spread over the combined shares; accretion is arithmetic, not evidence of a good deal.

citation.ref: Ch. Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

concepts.subsection: Foreign exchange — money market hedge
concepts.statement: A money market hedge manufactures a forward rate from the two interest rates: an exporter awaiting foreign currency borrows that currency today against the receivable, converts at spot, and invests at home; the foreign loan is repaid by the receivable itself. If interest rate parity holds exactly, the locked-in rate equals the forward rate and the choice is a matter of transaction cost and access, not principle.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.subsection: Risk management — Value at Risk
concepts.statement: Value at Risk states the largest loss expected over a stated horizon at a stated confidence — a one-day 99 per cent VaR of ₹10 lakh means one trading day in a hundred should lose more than ₹10 lakh. It says nothing about how much worse that hundredth day gets, which is the measure's famous blind spot.

concepts.subsection: Capital market line and security market line
concepts.statement: The capital market line prices total risk (standard deviation) and holds only efficient portfolios — combinations of the risk-free asset and the market portfolio. The security market line prices systematic risk (beta) and holds every fairly priced asset, efficient or not. A single stock full of diversifiable risk plots on the SML yet below the CML.

concepts.subsection: Dividend policy — MM irrelevance
concepts.statement: Modigliani and Miller hold that in a perfect market — no taxes, no transaction costs, no information gaps — dividend policy cannot change shareholder wealth: paying a dividend drops the ex-dividend price by the same amount, and a shareholder wanting cash can manufacture a dividend by selling shares. Real-world relevance arguments live exactly in the frictions the proof assumes away — taxes, signalling, clientele effects.

concepts.subsection: Interest rate swaps
concepts.statement: In a plain vanilla interest rate swap one party pays fixed and receives floating on a notional principal that is never exchanged; only net interest differences change hands each period. A borrower with floating-rate debt who pays fixed on a swap has synthetically fixed its cost; the swap's value at inception is zero and moves as rates move.

concepts.subsection: Foreign exchange — cross rates and triangular arbitrage
concepts.statement: Three currencies imply each cross rate from the other two; when a quoted cross rate strays from the implied rate, riding the three legs in the right circle returns more of the starting currency than was put in, risk-free. The direction matters — one way round the triangle profits, the other way loses — and the trade itself pushes the quotes back into line.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.subsection: Corporate valuation — FCFF and FCFE
concepts.statement: Free cash flow to the firm belongs to all capital providers and discounts at the weighted average cost of capital to give enterprise value; free cash flow to equity — FCFF less after-tax interest and net debt repayments — belongs to shareholders alone and discounts at the cost of equity to give equity value directly. Mixing a flow with the other side's discount rate is the classic valuation error.

concepts.subsection: Risk in capital budgeting — certainty equivalents
concepts.statement: The certainty equivalent approach shrinks each risky cash flow to the certain amount the decision-maker would accept instead, then discounts at the risk-free rate; the risk-adjusted discount rate approach keeps the expected flows and loads the risk into a higher rate. The rate route compounds the risk penalty with time even when risk does not grow; certainty equivalents price each year's risk on its own.

concepts.subsection: International capital budgeting — currency consistency
concepts.statement: A foreign project can be valued two ways that must agree: discount foreign currency cash flows at the foreign discount rate and convert the NPV at spot, or convert each year's flows at expected forward rates and discount in home currency at the home rate. Mixing — foreign flows with the home rate, or forwards with the foreign rate — builds the currency premium in twice or not at all.

concepts.subsection: Bond portfolio immunisation
concepts.statement: A bond portfolio is immunised against interest rate moves by matching its duration to the investment horizon: a rate rise then costs price but earns more on reinvested coupons, a fall does the reverse, and at the horizon the two effects offset. The match decays as time passes and rates move — durations drift at different speeds — so immunisation needs periodic rebalancing, not a one-time set-up.

concepts.subsection: Option strategies — protective put and covered call
concepts.statement: A protective put — stock plus a bought put — buys insurance: losses stop at the strike, the upside stays open, and the premium is the cost of certainty. A covered call — stock plus a sold call — sells the upside: the premium is income, gains cap at the strike, and the downside stays open less the premium. One pays to remove tail risk; the other is paid to surrender tail gain.

concepts.subsection: Currency swaps
concepts.statement: A currency swap exchanges principal and interest in one currency for principal and interest in another — and unlike an interest rate swap, the principals are real: exchanged at the start (or notionally referenced) and re-exchanged at maturity at the original rate, which is where the currency risk transfers. Each party ends up servicing debt in the currency it wanted, having first borrowed where its **comparative** advantage lies — the market where its own borrowing spread against the other party is widest, which is not always the market where it borrows cheapest in absolute terms.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.subsection: Arbitrage pricing theory
concepts.statement: APT prices assets from several systematic factors — industrial production, inflation surprises, interest rates, credit spreads — each with its own beta and premium, where CAPM compresses all systematic risk into one market beta. APT's discipline is arbitrage: two portfolios with identical factor exposures must earn identical expected returns, or the difference is picked up risk-free. It says nothing about which factors — that is empirical.

concepts.subsection: Lease versus buy evaluation
concepts.statement: Lease-or-buy is a financing comparison, so its cash flows — lease rentals net of tax shield, forgone depreciation shields, salvage forgone — discount at the after-tax cost of debt, not the project's cost of capital: the lease displaces borrowing of equivalent risk. The investment decision comes first and separately; a bad project is not rescued by a clever lease.

concepts.subsection: Securitisation
concepts.statement: Securitisation sells a pool of receivables to a bankruptcy-remote special purpose vehicle that funds the purchase by issuing securities serviced by the pool's collections. True sale takes the assets off the originator's balance sheet; tranching splits the paper into senior, mezzanine and equity slices absorbing losses bottom-up; credit enhancement — overcollateralisation, subordination, guarantees — lifts the senior tranche's rating above the originator's own.

concepts.subsection: Startup finance — funding stages
concepts.statement: Startup money arrives in stages priced to risk: bootstrapping and friends-and-family at the idea, angels at the prototype, venture capital in lettered rounds as revenue proves out, and strategic or public markets at maturity. Each round prices the company anew — pre-money plus new cash equals post-money — and earlier holders dilute unless they follow on. Venture investors buy convertible preferred with liquidation preference, anti-dilution and board rights, not plain equity.

concepts.subsection: Types of foreign exchange exposure
concepts.statement: Transaction exposure is a booked receivable or payable awaiting settlement — hedgeable with forwards and options. Translation exposure is the accounting restatement of foreign subsidiaries' balances at consolidation — a reporting effect with no cash flow of its own. Economic exposure is the deepest: the effect of exchange rates on future competitiveness and cash flows, reaching even firms that never invoice abroad, and managed by operational choices more than by derivatives.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.subsection: Mutual funds — costs and tracking error
concepts.statement: The expense ratio is deducted from the fund's assets daily, so investors earn the portfolio's return minus costs — a one-and-a-half per cent ratio on an eight per cent market compounds into a fifth of the wealth over decades. For index funds the second report card is tracking error: the volatility of the fund's return differences against its benchmark. Low fees with faithful tracking is the entire proposition of passive investing.

concepts.subsection: Futures — margins and marking to market
concepts.statement: A futures position opens with initial margin and is marked to market daily — losses are debited and gains credited to the margin account each evening at the settlement price. When the balance falls below the maintenance margin, a margin call demands topping back up to the initial level; failure triggers position closure. Daily settlement is why futures carry negligible counterparty risk and why they can bankrupt a trader long before expiry.

concepts.subsection: Interest rate caps, floors and collars
concepts.statement: A cap pays the borrower whenever the reference rate fixes above the strike — insurance against rising rates, bought for a premium; a floor pays the lender when rates fix below its strike. A borrower's collar buys a cap and sells a floor, financing the protection by surrendering the benefit of falls below the floor — at zero net cost when the strikes are chosen so the premiums offset. The borrower's rate then lives inside a band.

concepts.subsection: Economic value added
concepts.statement: EVA charges profit for all the capital that earned it: net operating profit after tax minus the capital employed times its weighted average cost. A company can grow accounting profit every year while destroying value, if the new profit earns less than the capital's cost. Positive EVA — return on capital above WACC — is what accounting profit alone never certifies.

concepts.subsection: SA 300 — Planning an Audit of Financial Statements
concepts.statement: The overall audit strategy sets the scope, timing and direction of the audit and guides the development of the more detailed audit plan; the plan converts the strategy into the specific nature, timing and extent of risk assessment procedures and further audit procedures at the assertion level. The two remain interrelated after they are first set — changes discovered while developing the plan can send the auditor back to revise the strategy — and planning continues as an iterative process throughout the audit rather than ending as a discrete opening phase.

citation.ref: Overall audit strategy and the audit plan

concepts.subsection: SA 402 — Audit Considerations Relating to an Entity Using a Service Organisation
concepts.statement: Where the auditor uses evidence from a service organisation's type 1 or type 2 report, the auditor's report on the user entity's financial statements does not refer to that service auditor's report — doing so could be misread as dividing responsibility, which the user auditor may not do. A reference is made only where law or regulation requires it, and even then the report states that the reference does not reduce the user auditor's own responsibility for the opinion expressed.

citation.ref: Reference to a service auditor in the auditor's report

concepts.subsection: SA 450 — Evaluation of Misstatements Identified during the Audit
concepts.statement: The auditor accumulates every misstatement identified during the audit other than those that are clearly trivial — a threshold set well below materiality, catching only amounts that are inconsequential in size and nature, individually and in aggregate, beyond any reasonable doubt. Where there is any uncertainty about whether an item is clearly trivial, the auditor treats it as not clearly trivial and accumulates it.

concepts.subsection: SA 500 — Audit Evidence
concepts.statement: A management's expert is an individual or organisation with expertise in a field other than accounting or auditing whose work is used by the entity to help prepare the financial statements. Before relying on that work as audit evidence, the auditor evaluates the expert's competence, capabilities and objectivity; obtains an understanding of the expert's field sufficient to evaluate the work; and evaluates the appropriateness of the work, including the source data, methods and assumptions used, as evidence for the relevant assertion.

citation.ref: Using the work of a management's expert

concepts.subsection: SA 540 (Revised) — Auditing Accounting Estimates
concepts.statement: Accounting estimates sit on a spectrum of inherent risk: some carry low estimation uncertainty and complexity — a straightforward provision computed from a fixed formula — while others, such as an expected credit loss model or a goodwill impairment test, carry high estimation uncertainty, subjectivity and susceptibility to management bias. The auditor's response scales with where an estimate sits on that spectrum: the rigour applied to testing methods, data, assumptions and indicators of bias rises with the estimate's complexity rather than staying uniform across every estimate in the file.

concepts.subsection: CARO 2020 — Clause 3(i)
concepts.statement: Clause 3(i) covers property, plant and equipment: whether the company maintains proper records showing full particulars, including quantitative details and situation, of PPE and intangible assets; whether PPE is physically verified by management at reasonable intervals with discrepancies properly dealt with in the books; whether title deeds of immovable property are held in the company's own name, with details where not; and whether any revaluation was carried out, based on a registered valuer's valuation, with the quantum of change specified where the change is 10 per cent or more of the net carrying value.

concepts.subsection: CARO 2020 — Clause 3(vii)
concepts.statement: Clause 3(vii) asks whether the company is regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues — GST, provident fund, employees' state insurance, income tax and other applicable dues — with the appropriate authorities, stating the extent of arrears outstanding as at the balance sheet date for a period of more than six months from the date they became payable; it separately asks for disputed statutory dues not deposited, with the amount involved and the forum where the dispute is pending.

concepts.subsection: CARO 2020 — Clause 3(ix)
concepts.statement: Clause 3(ix) covers repayment discipline: whether the company defaulted in repayment of loans or other borrowings, or in payment of interest, to any lender, with the period and amount of default; whether the company has been declared a wilful defaulter by any bank, financial institution or lender; whether term loans were applied for the purpose for which they were obtained, with the amount and details of any diversion; and whether funds raised on a short-term basis were used for long-term purposes.

concepts.subsection: First Schedule Part I — Clause 3
concepts.statement: Clause 3 of Part I of the First Schedule bars a member in practice from accepting or agreeing to accept any part of the profits of the professional work of a person who is not a member of the Institute. The Council has carved a limited exception for prescribed reciprocal arrangements with certain other recognised professional bodies; outside that carve-out, sharing professional profits with a non-member is misconduct regardless of the non-member's own standing or the quality of the work referred.

concepts.subsection: First Schedule Part I — Clause 4
concepts.statement: Clause 4 of Part I of the First Schedule bars a member in practice from entering into partnership, in or outside India, with any person other than a chartered accountant in practice, unless that person belongs to a professional body the Council has notified as permitted — company secretaries, cost accountants, advocates enrolled with a Bar Council, architects and actuaries among them — subject to the Council's conditions for such multidisciplinary partnerships.

concepts.subsection: Section 143(3)(i) — Internal financial controls reporting
concepts.statement: Section 143(3)(i) requires the statutory auditor's report to state whether the company has an adequate internal financial controls system with reference to the financial statements in place, and whether it operated effectively — a separate opinion from the opinion on the financial statements themselves. MCA notification G.S.R. 583(E) dated 13 June 2017 lifts that reporting for a private company which is a one person company or a small company, or whose turnover is less than ₹50 crore as per the latest audited financial statement and whose aggregate borrowings from banks, financial institutions or any body corporate at any point during the financial year are less than ₹25 crore. The notification as first published put an "or" between those two figures; a corrigendum dated 13 July 2017 replaced it with "and", so both must hold. The exemption is forfeited entirely if the company has defaulted in filing its financial statements under section 137 or its annual return under section 92.

citation.ref: Section 143(3)(i), read with entry 9A and paragraph 2A of MCA Notification G.S.R. 583(E) dated 13.06.2017 (amending G.S.R. 464(E) dated 05.06.2015, issued under section 462) and the corrigendum thereto dated 13.07.2017

concepts.subsection: Companies (Accounts) Rules — Audit trail
concepts.statement: Every company using accounting software to maintain its books must use software carrying an audit trail (edit log) feature that records every transaction, logs every change made to it, and cannot be disabled — mandatory from financial years commencing on or after 1 April 2023. The statutory auditor separately reports whether such software was used throughout the year, whether the audit trail feature operated for all transactions without being tampered with, and whether the audit trail has been preserved as required by the statutory record-retention period.

concepts.subsection: Audit of consolidated financial statements — materiality
concepts.statement: In an audit of consolidated financial statements the auditor computes materiality for the group as a whole, and uses that group materiality to assess whether the permanent and current period consolidation adjustments made by the parent's management are appropriate, and to judge which components are material enough to be scoped in. The principal auditor also computes materiality for each component and communicates it to the component auditor where he believes that is required for a true and fair view on the consolidated financial statements. Materiality for a component's own standalone opinion is computed component-wise on a standalone basis by that component's auditor, for a different opinion, and it does not become the group's materiality.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: Materiality in the audit of consolidated financial statements

concepts.subsection: Audit of consolidated financial statements — consolidation adjustments
concepts.statement: Permanent consolidation adjustments are made only on the first occasion of consolidation, or on a later occasion when the shareholding in a consolidated entity changes: determining goodwill or capital reserve, and determining the amount of equity attributable to the minority or non-controlling interests. The auditor pays particular attention to the pre-acquisition reserves and the dates of investment, and to whether pre-acquisition reserves have been allocated correctly between the parent and the minority. Current period consolidation adjustments are made in the period being consolidated and relate mainly to eliminating intra-group transactions and balances — intra-group interest and management fees, unrealised intra-group profits on assets transferred between components, deferred tax on those eliminations, intra-group indebtedness, harmonising different accounting policies, and adjustments for recognised subsequent events.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: Permanent consolidation adjustments and current period consolidation adjustments

concepts.subsection: Audit of consolidated financial statements — a component on a different framework
concepts.statement: Where a component prepares its financial statements under an accounting framework different from the parent's — a foreign subsidiary on US GAAP, IFRS or a local GAAP — the parent's management performs the conversion of the component's audited financial statements to the framework used for the consolidated financial statements, and the principal auditor audits those conversion adjustments so that the component's financial information is suitable for consolidation. The alternative route is for the component to report against the group accounting manual, in which case the principal auditor performs procedures to determine that the group accounting policies comply with the GAAP applicable to the parent. On the auditing side, for the parent auditor to rely on and refer to the component auditor's report, the component's financial statements should have been audited under a framework corresponding to Indian GAAS.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: Component auditor reporting under an accounting or auditing framework different from the parent's

concepts.subsection: Audit of consolidated financial statements — an unaudited component
concepts.statement: Where the financial statements of one or more components remain unaudited, the auditor reporting on the consolidated financial statements evaluates both the qualitative and the quantitative factors bearing on the amounts left unaudited, and considers a modification of the opinion under SA 705, because sufficient appropriate audit evidence has not been obtained for those consolidated balances. An unaudited component is not dropped out of the consolidation, and an Emphasis of Matter paragraph does not cure missing evidence.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: Components not audited — evaluation of a possible modification under SA 705

concepts.subsection: SSAE 3000 — Assurance Engagements on Sustainability Information
concepts.statement: SSAE 3000, Assurance Engagements on Sustainability Information, issued by ICAI, is the umbrella standard for every assurance engagement on an entity's sustainability information, and it covers engagements giving either reasonable assurance or limited assurance. It applied on a voluntary basis to assurance reports covering periods ending on 31 March 2023, and on a mandatory basis to assurance reports covering periods ending on or after 31 March 2024. Assurance on a greenhouse gas statement is dealt with separately by SAE 3410, Assurance Engagements on Greenhouse Gas Statements.

citation.ref: Scope of the Standard and effective date of application

concepts.subsection: BRSR — essential and leadership indicators
concepts.statement: The Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report is mandatory from financial year 2022-23, having been voluntary in 2021-22, and SEBI has started with the top 1,000 listed companies by market capitalisation. It has three sections: Section A, general disclosures about the entity, its products, operations, employees and group companies; Section B, management process and policy disclosures covering governance, leadership and oversight; and Section C, principle-wise performance disclosures against the nine principles of the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct. Section C splits its key performance indicators in two — essential indicators, which are mandatory disclosures, and leadership indicators, which are optional.

citation.ref: Regulation 34(2)(f) read with the prescribed BRSR format, Sections A, B and C

concepts.subsection: Climate-related risks in an audit of financial statements
concepts.statement: Climate-related risks belong inside the auditor's understanding of the entity, and matter more in some sectors than others — banking and insurance, energy, transportation, materials and buildings, agriculture, food and forestry products. Before considering any reference to climate in the auditor's report, the auditor determines whether the entity has appropriately disclosed the relevant climate-related information in the financial statements under the applicable financial reporting framework, because a climate commitment is frequently evidence about an estimate already in those statements — a useful life, an impairment, a decommissioning provision. Where a climate disclosure in the financial statements is of fundamental importance to users' understanding, an Emphasis of Matter paragraph may be warranted; climate narrative sitting elsewhere in the annual report is other information, read for consistency, and carries no opinion.

citation.ref: Ch. Sustainable Development Goals and ESG Assurance — role of the auditor, consideration of climate-related risks

concepts.subsection: SEBI LODR Regulation 18 — audit committee composition and meetings
concepts.statement: Every listed entity constitutes a qualified and independent audit committee of at least three directors, of whom two-thirds are independent directors; where the entity has outstanding superior rights (SR) equity shares, the audit committee comprises only independent directors. Every member is financially literate — able to read and understand a balance sheet, a profit and loss account and a statement of cash flows — and at least one member has accounting or related financial management expertise. The chairperson is an independent director and is present at the annual general meeting to answer shareholder queries, and the company secretary acts as secretary to the committee. The committee meets at least four times a year with not more than one hundred and twenty days between two meetings, and the quorum is two members or one-third of the members, whichever is greater, with a minimum of two independent directors present.

concepts.subsection: Section 177(7) — the auditor's right to be heard in the audit committee
concepts.statement: Section 177(7) gives the auditors of a company and its key managerial personnel a right to be heard in the meetings of the audit committee when the committee considers the auditor's report, but no right to vote. Regulation 18(1) of the LODR Regulations separately has a representative of the statutory auditor invited to audit committee meetings when required, while allowing the committee occasionally to meet without any executive of the listed entity present. Under Section 177(8), the Board's report under Section 134(3) discloses the composition of the audit committee and, where the Board has not accepted a recommendation of the audit committee, that fact along with the reasons for it.

concepts.subsection: Certificate on compliance of conditions of corporate governance
concepts.statement: A listed entity obtains a compliance certificate on compliance with the conditions of corporate governance from either its auditors or a practising company secretary, and annexes it to the directors' report. The auditor's responsibility is the verification and certification of the factual implementation of the conditions stipulated in the LODR Regulations: it is neither an audit nor an expression of opinion on the financial statements, and it is neither an assurance as to the future viability of the company nor as to the efficiency or effectiveness with which management has conducted the company's affairs. The work is carried out under the Guidance Note on Certification of Corporate Governance, with documentation under SA 230 and management representations under SA 580. Facts such as an audit committee that did not meet four times, or a chairman of the audit committee who is not an independent director, call for an adverse or qualified statement in the certificate.

citation.ref: Regulation 34(3) read with Schedule V — compliance certificate on conditions of corporate governance

concepts.subsection: Section 143(6) — CAG supplementary audit of a government company
concepts.statement: In a government company the Comptroller and Auditor-General appoints the auditor under Section 139(5) or Section 139(7) and directs the manner in which the accounts are to be audited; the auditor then submits a copy of his audit report to the CAG, and that copy includes the CAG's directions, the action taken on them, and their impact on the accounts and financial statement of the company. Section 143(6) gives the CAG, within sixty days from the date of receipt of that audit report, a right to conduct a supplementary audit through persons he authorises and to comment upon or supplement the audit report; the comments or supplement are sent by the company to every person entitled to copies of the audited financial statements under Section 136(1) and are placed before the annual general meeting at the same time and in the same manner as the audit report. Section 143(7) separately allows the CAG to order a test audit.

citation.ref: Section 143(5), Section 143(6) and the proviso to Section 143(6), and Section 143(7)

concepts.subsection: SQC 1 — retention of engagement documentation
concepts.statement: SQC 1 requires the firm to establish policies and procedures for the retention of engagement documentation, and in the specific case of audit engagements the retention period is ordinarily no shorter than seven years from the date of the auditor's report or, if later, the date of the group auditor's report. This is a firm-level retention obligation running from a report date, and it is separate from the SA 230 requirement to complete the administrative assembly of the final audit file ordinarily within not more than sixty days after the date of the auditor's report.

citation.ref: para 83 — retention period for engagement documentation

concepts.subsection: Advances — provisioning norms
concepts.statement: Provisioning follows classification. A substandard asset carries a general provision of 15 per cent of the total outstanding, made without any allowance for ECGC guarantee cover or securities available, and an unsecured exposure identified as substandard carries an additional 10 per cent — 25 per cent in all. On a doubtful asset the extent not covered by the realisable value of the security carries 100 per cent, and the secured portion carries 25 per cent where the asset has remained doubtful up to one year, 40 per cent for one to three years, and 100 per cent beyond three years. A loss asset should be written off, and if it is permitted to remain on the books, 100 per cent of the outstanding is provided.

citation.ref: Prudential norms on IRACP — paras 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4

concepts.subsection: Section 212 — investigation by the Serious Fraud Investigation Office
concepts.statement: Under Section 212(1) the Central Government may, by order, assign an investigation into a company's affairs to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office on receipt of a report of the Registrar or an inspector under Section 208, on intimation of a special resolution passed by the company that its affairs are required to be investigated, in the public interest, or on a request from any Department of the Central Government or a State Government. Once a case is so assigned, Section 212(2) bars any other investigating agency of the Central Government or of any State Government from proceeding with an investigation in that case in respect of an offence under the Act; an investigation already initiated is not proceeded with further, and the agency concerned transfers the relevant documents and records to the SFIO.

concepts.subsection: SA 230 — Audit Documentation
concepts.statement: An auditor complies with each requirement of an SA unless the whole SA is not relevant, or the requirement is not relevant because it is conditional and the condition does not exist. In exceptional circumstances the auditor may judge it necessary to depart from a relevant requirement, and must then perform alternative audit procedures to achieve the aim of that requirement. SA 230 makes the departure visible rather than silent: the auditor documents how the alternative audit procedures performed achieve the aim of the requirement, and the reasons for the departure. The same standard requires the file to record the identifying characteristics of the specific items or matters tested, who performed the audit work and the date the work was completed, and who reviewed the audit work performed and the date and extent of that review.

citation.ref: para 9 and para 12, read with SA 200 para 23

concepts.subsection: SA 620 — Using the Work of an Auditor's Expert
concepts.statement: Satisfying himself about the competence, capabilities and objectivity of the auditor's expert is only the entry ticket. The auditor then evaluates the adequacy of the expert's work for the auditor's purposes: the relevance and reasonableness of that expert's findings or conclusions and their consistency with other audit evidence; where the work uses significant assumptions and methods, the relevance and reasonableness of those assumptions and methods in the circumstances; and where the work uses source data significant to it, the relevance, completeness and accuracy of that source data. If the work is not adequate for the auditor's purposes, the auditor agrees with that expert on the nature and extent of further work to be performed by the expert, or performs additional audit procedures appropriate to the circumstances.

concepts.subsection: SA 510 — Initial Audit Engagements: Opening Balances
concepts.statement: SA 510 separates the two reasons an opening balance damages the current opinion. Where the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence regarding the opening balances, the opinion is qualified or disclaimed, as appropriate. Where the opening balances contain a misstatement that materially affects the current period's financial statements and the effect is not properly accounted for or not adequately presented or disclosed, the opinion is qualified or adverse. The same qualified-or-adverse answer applies where the current period's accounting policies are not consistently applied in relation to the opening balances, or where a change is not properly accounted for, presented or disclosed. And where the predecessor auditor's opinion was modified and the matter remains relevant and material to the current period's financial statements, the auditor modifies his own opinion on the current period's financial statements — an Other Matter paragraph recording what the predecessor said does not discharge it.

concepts.subsection: SA 710 — Comparative Information: Corresponding Figures
concepts.statement: Where the prior period's financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor and the auditor is not prohibited by law or regulation from referring to that report, the auditor states in an Other Matter paragraph that the corresponding figures were audited by the predecessor auditor, the type of opinion the predecessor expressed and, if that opinion was modified, the reasons for the modification, and the date of that report. Where the prior period's financial statements were not audited at all, the auditor states in an Other Matter paragraph that the corresponding figures are unaudited. Saying so does not relieve the auditor of the requirement to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence that the opening balances do not contain misstatements that materially affect the current period's financial statements.

concepts.subsection: SA 520 — Analytical Procedures
concepts.statement: A substantive analytical procedure is only as good as four things the auditor must settle before it is run. The auditor determines the suitability of the particular procedure for the given assertions, taking account of the assessed risks of material misstatement and of any tests of details for those assertions; evaluates the reliability of the data from which the expectation is developed, taking account of its source, comparability, nature and relevance and the controls over its preparation; develops an expectation of recorded amounts or ratios sufficiently precise to identify a misstatement that, individually or when aggregated with others, may cause the financial statements to be materially misstated; and determines the amount of any difference of recorded amounts from expected values that is acceptable without further investigation. Where the results show fluctuations or relationships inconsistent with other relevant information, or that differ from expected values by a significant amount, the auditor investigates by inquiring of management, obtaining appropriate audit evidence relevant to management's responses, and performing other audit procedures as necessary.

concepts.subsection: SA 530 — Audit Sampling
concepts.statement: An anomaly is a misstatement or deviation that is demonstrably not representative of misstatements or deviations in a population. The label is available only in extremely rare circumstances, and only where the auditor has obtained a high degree of certainty that the misstatement or deviation is not representative of the population — a certainty obtained by performing additional audit procedures sufficient to provide it, not by accepting management's explanation of the cause. An anomalous misstatement may then be left out when projecting misstatements from the sample to the population, but the misstatement itself does not disappear: its own effect, if uncorrected, is still added to the projected misstatement of the rest when the auditor evaluates the results of the sample.

concepts.subsection: SA 560 — Subsequent Events
concepts.statement: After the financial statements have been issued the auditor has no obligation to perform any audit procedures on them. But if a fact then becomes known that, had it been known at the date of the auditor's report, may have caused the auditor to amend that report, the auditor discusses the matter with management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance, determines whether the financial statements need amendment and, if so, inquires how management intends to address the matter. Where management amends, the auditor carries out the audit procedures necessary in the circumstances on the amendment, reviews the steps management takes to ensure that anyone in receipt of the previously issued financial statements together with the auditor's report on them is informed, and issues a new or amended auditor's report that includes an Emphasis of Matter paragraph or Other Matter paragraph referring to a note that more extensively discusses the reason for the amendment and to the earlier report. Where management does not take those steps and does not amend the financial statements, the auditor notifies management and those charged with governance that he will seek to prevent future reliance on the auditor's report, and if they still do not act, takes appropriate action to seek to prevent that reliance.

concepts.subsection: SA 580 — Written Representations
concepts.statement: The written representations are dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report, and cover all financial statements and periods referred to in that report. If management does not provide one or more of the requested representations, the auditor discusses the matter with management, re-evaluates the integrity of management and the effect that has on the reliability of representations and of audit evidence in general, and takes appropriate actions including the possible effect on the opinion. Two situations are answered by a disclaimer of opinion rather than by a qualification: where the auditor concludes that there is sufficient doubt about the integrity of management such that the representations about management's own responsibilities are not reliable, and where management simply does not provide those representations — that it has fulfilled its responsibility for the preparation of the financial statements, and that it has provided the auditor with all relevant information and access agreed in the terms of the audit engagement.

concepts.subsection: SA 550 — Related Parties
concepts.statement: Where the auditor identifies related parties or significant related party transactions that management has not previously identified or disclosed to the auditor, the response is a set of six steps, not a disclosure edit. The auditor promptly communicates the relevant information to the other members of the engagement team; requests management to identify all transactions with the newly identified related parties for the auditor's further evaluation; inquires why the entity's controls over related party relationships and transactions failed to enable the identification or disclosure; performs appropriate substantive audit procedures on the newly identified related parties or significant related party transactions; reconsiders the risk that other related parties or significant related party transactions may exist that management has not disclosed, and performs additional audit procedures as necessary; and where the non-disclosure by management appears intentional, and is therefore indicative of a risk of material misstatement due to fraud, evaluates the implications for the audit.

concepts.subsection: SA 250 — Consideration of Laws and Regulations
concepts.statement: Where the auditor suspects that management or those charged with governance are involved in non-compliance, the auditor communicates the matter to the next higher level of authority at the entity if one exists, such as the audit committee or the supervisory board; where no higher authority exists, or where the auditor believes the communication may not be acted upon or is unsure to whom to report, the auditor considers the need to obtain legal advice. The reporting consequence then splits on what went wrong. Where the auditor concludes that the non-compliance has a material effect on the financial statements and has not been adequately reflected in them, the opinion is qualified or adverse. Where the auditor is precluded by management or those charged with governance from obtaining sufficient appropriate audit evidence to evaluate whether non-compliance that may be material has, or is likely to have, occurred, the opinion is qualified or disclaimed on the basis of a limitation on the scope of the audit.

citation.ref: reporting to a higher level of authority and the implications for the opinion — paras 23, 24 and 25

concepts.subsection: SA 501 — Audit Evidence: Litigation and Claims
concepts.statement: The auditor designs and performs audit procedures to identify litigation and claims involving the entity which may give rise to a risk of material misstatement, including inquiry of management and, where applicable, others within the entity including in-house legal counsel; reviewing minutes of meetings of those charged with governance and correspondence between the entity and its external legal counsel; and reviewing legal expense accounts. Where the auditor assesses a risk of material misstatement regarding litigation or claims that have been identified, or where procedures indicate that other material litigation or claims may exist, the auditor seeks direct communication with the entity's external legal counsel through a letter of inquiry prepared by management and sent by the auditor, asking the external legal counsel to communicate directly with the auditor. Where management refuses to give that permission, or the external legal counsel refuses to respond appropriately or is prohibited from responding, and the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence by performing alternative audit procedures, the auditor modifies the opinion.

concepts.subsection: SA 240 — The Auditor's Responsibilities Relating to Fraud
concepts.statement: Where the auditor has identified a fraud or has obtained information that indicates a fraud may exist, he communicates these matters on a timely basis to the appropriate level of management — ordinarily at least one level above the persons who appear to be involved. Where the auditor identifies or suspects fraud involving management, employees who have significant roles in internal control, or others where the fraud results in a material misstatement in the financial statements, he communicates these matters to those charged with governance on a timely basis. Where a misstatement resulting from fraud or suspected fraud brings the auditor's ability to continue performing the audit into question, the auditor determines the professional and legal responsibilities applicable in the circumstances, considers whether to withdraw where withdrawal is possible under applicable law, and if he withdraws, discusses the withdrawal and its reasons with the appropriate level of management and those charged with governance and determines whether there is a professional or legal requirement to report the withdrawal and its reasons to the persons who made the audit appointment or to regulatory authorities. The professional duty of confidentiality may be overridden by law, and the auditor may take legal advice on where that line falls.

concepts.subsection: Section 143(12) with Rule 13 — the mechanics of reporting a fraud
concepts.statement: Where the auditor has reason to believe that an offence of fraud involving, or expected to involve individually, an amount of one crore rupees or above is being or has been committed against the company by its officers or employees, he reports the matter to the Central Government by a fixed route. He first reports to the Board or the Audit Committee immediately but not later than two days of his knowledge of the fraud, seeking their reply or observations within forty-five days. On receiving that reply he forwards his report, the reply or observations, and his own comments on them, to the Central Government within fifteen days of receiving the reply. Where no reply or observations come within the forty-five days, he forwards his report to the Central Government along with a note containing the details of the report earlier sent and not replied to. The report goes to the Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs in a sealed cover by registered post with acknowledgement due or by speed post followed by an email in confirmation, on the auditor's letterhead, signed with his seal and quoting his membership number, in the form of the statement specified in Form ADT-4. Where the fraud is below one crore rupees, it goes to the Audit Committee constituted under section 177 or to the Board within the same two days, stating the nature of the fraud with description, the approximate amount involved and the parties involved, and those details are then disclosed in the Board's report.

citation.ref: Section 143(12) read with Rule 13(1), Rule 13(2) and Rule 13(3) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014

concepts.subsection: Sections 21A and 21B — the Board of Discipline and the Disciplinary Committee
concepts.statement: Which forum hears a case is decided by which Schedule the misconduct sits in, and the Director (Discipline) makes that routing after forming a prima facie opinion on the complaint or information. A case of misconduct falling under the First Schedule goes before the Board of Discipline. A case falling under the Second Schedule, or under both the Schedules, goes before the Disciplinary Committee. The powers differ with the forum. On holding a member guilty under the First Schedule, the Board of Discipline may reprimand the member, remove his name from the Register of Members for a period not exceeding three months, or impose a fine. On holding a member guilty under the Second Schedule or under both Schedules, the Disciplinary Committee may reprimand the member, remove his name from the Register of Members permanently or for such period as it thinks fit, or impose a fine. Permanent removal belongs to the Disciplinary Committee alone, and the Director (Discipline) punishes nobody.

citation.ref: Section 21A(3) and Section 21B(3), read with the routing under Section 21(3)

concepts.subsection: SA 260 (Revised) — Communication with Those Charged with Governance
concepts.statement: Planning communication and findings communication are two different requirements, and the second is a named list. The auditor communicates to those charged with governance his views about significant qualitative aspects of the entity's accounting practices, including accounting policies, accounting estimates and financial statement disclosures; significant difficulties, if any, encountered during the audit; unless all of those charged with governance are involved in managing the entity, significant matters arising during the audit that were discussed with, or subject to correspondence with, management, and the written representations the auditor is requesting; circumstances that affect the form and content of the auditor's report; and any other significant matters relevant to the oversight of the financial reporting process. Significant findings are communicated in writing where, in the auditor's professional judgement, oral communication would not be adequate. None of it is conditional on the opinion turning out modified, and telling management is not telling those charged with governance.

concepts.subsection: SA 265 — Communicating Deficiencies in Internal Control
concepts.statement: A significant deficiency does not stop at those charged with governance. SA 265 sends it in writing to those charged with governance and, separately and also in writing, to management at an appropriate level of responsibility; other deficiencies of sufficient importance to merit management's attention go to management alone. The written communication of a significant deficiency has a prescribed content. It carries a description of the deficiencies and an explanation of their potential effects, and sufficient information to enable those charged with governance and management to understand the context of the communication — namely that the purpose of the audit was to express an opinion on the financial statements, that the audit considered internal control relevant to the preparation of the financial statements in order to design audit procedures appropriate in the circumstances but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of internal control, and that the matters reported are limited to those deficiencies identified during the audit and concluded to be of sufficient importance to merit being reported.

concepts.subsection: SA 402 — Audit Considerations Relating to an Entity Using a Service Organisation
concepts.statement: A complementary user entity control is a control that the service organisation assumes, in the design of its service, will be implemented by user entities, and which is identified in the description of its system if it is necessary to achieve the stated control objectives. It does not sit at the service organisation, so the service auditor never tests it.
