Falling short, the trust may accumulate for up to five years for a specific purpose by filing the prescribed statement, or treat income received late as applied when actually spent. Application now counts on payment, not accrual.

concepts.subsection: Section 50B — Slump sale
concepts.statement: A slump sale transfers an undertaking as a going concern for a lump sum without itemised values; capital gain is the deemed consideration — the fair market value computed under the rules — less the undertaking's net worth as cost of acquisition, with net worth computed on the prescribed basis, ignoring revaluations. An undertaking held over thirty-six months yields long-term gain even though depreciable assets ride inside it.

concepts.subsection: Section 194R — TDS on business perquisites
concepts.statement: A person providing any benefit or perquisite arising from business or profession — foreign trips for dealers, gifted cars, sponsored gadgets, waived debts — deducts ten per cent of its value, where the aggregate to a recipient exceeds twenty thousand rupees in the year. The deduction applies whether the benefit is in cash or kind or partly both, and for benefits wholly in kind the provider must ensure tax is paid before releasing them.

concepts.subsection: Section 35 — Scientific research expenditure
concepts.statement: In-house scientific research related to the business earns deduction of both revenue and capital expenditure — land excluded — in the year incurred; pre-commencement research expenditure of the three prior years is deductible in the year business begins. The weighted deductions of the past have sunset to one hundred per cent, and contributions to approved institutions ride their own approval-dependent limbs.

concepts.subsection: Corporate residence — place of effective management
concepts.statement: A foreign company is resident in India if its place of effective management — where key management and commercial decisions necessary for the business as a whole are in substance made — is in India that year. Board meetings held abroad do not settle it when the board merely ratifies decisions taken in India; conversely, active regional headquarters abroad making the decisions keep POEM outside. The test is substance over minutes.

concepts.subsection: Appeals — Commissioner (Appeals) powers
concepts.statement: The Commissioner (Appeals) may confirm, reduce, enhance or annul an assessment — the power to enhance makes the first appeal a two-edged forum, exercisable only after a reasonable opportunity to show cause. What the first appellate authority lacks is the power to set aside and remand the assessment for a fresh run; the appeal must be decided, point by point.

concepts.subsection: Buy-back proceeds as dividend — section 2(22)(f)
concepts.statement: For buy-backs on or after 1 October 2024, the company-level buy-back tax is gone: the entire consideration a shareholder receives is deemed a dividend under section 2(22)(f), taxable at slab rates with no deduction for cost, and subject to dividend TDS. The shares' cost is not lost — the transfer is computed with consideration deemed nil, manufacturing a capital loss that sets off and carries forward against capital gains only.

concepts.subsection: Deemed dividend — section 2(22)(e)
concepts.statement: A loan or advance by a closely held company to a shareholder holding ten per cent or more of voting power — or to a concern in which such a shareholder is substantially interested — is deemed a dividend to the extent of the company's accumulated profits. Repayment later does not undo the deeming; loans in the ordinary course of a money-lending business and certain set-offs escape it.

concepts.subsection: Section 73 — Speculation losses
concepts.statement: Speculation loss sets off only against speculation profit, and carries forward just four years. A speculative transaction settles otherwise than by actual delivery — but eligible exchange-traded derivatives are excluded from the definition, while the Explanation to section 73 deems a company's share-trading business speculative unless the company falls in the carved-out categories. Delivery-based investing and F&O thus sit outside; a company churning shares as a business sits inside.

concepts.subsection: Agricultural income — partial integration
concepts.statement: Agricultural income is exempt, but for individuals with net agricultural income above five thousand rupees and other income above the basic exemption, it enters the rate machinery: tax is computed on the aggregate, then reduced by tax on agricultural income plus the exemption limit. The farm income is never taxed itself — it pushes the other income into higher slabs. Companies and firms, taxed at flat rates, are outside the scheme.

citation.ref: Section 10(1) with Finance Act rate schedule

concepts.subsection: Section 43B — Deduction on actual payment
concepts.statement: Certain sums deduct only when actually paid, whatever the books accrue: taxes, duties and cesses, employer contributions to funds, bonus and commission to employees, interest to banks and financial institutions, and leave encashment among them. Payment by the return's due date saves the year's deduction; converting unpaid interest into a fresh loan is expressly not payment, and the deduction waits for the converted loan's actual repayment.

concepts.subsection: Section 194Q — TDS on purchase of goods
concepts.statement: A buyer whose turnover exceeded ten crore rupees in the preceding year deducts tax at 0.1 per cent on purchases from a resident seller beyond fifty lakh rupees in the year, deducting on the excess. The mirror-image seller-side TCS on goods stood omitted from 1 April 2025, ending the old overlap where the buyer's TDS took precedence — the buyer's obligation now stands alone. Failure invites the thirty per cent disallowance for TDS defaults.

citation.ref: Section 194Q (TCS on goods omitted w.e.f. 1 April 2025)

concepts.subsection: Section 54F — Investment of any LTCG in a house
concepts.statement: Long-term gain on any capital asset other than a residential house is exempt where the net consideration — not merely the gain — is invested in one residential house in India, proportionately where investment falls short, capped at ten crore rupees of investment. The gates: not owning more than one other residential house on the transfer date, and no second house purchase within the lock-in windows. Section 54, by contrast, covers house-to-house and asks only the gain to be reinvested.

concepts.subsection: Section 139(8A) — Updated returns
concepts.statement: An updated return may be filed within forty-eight months of the assessment year's end — the window doubled by the Finance Act 2025 — on payment of additional tax that climbs with delay: twenty-five per cent of tax and interest in the first twelve months, fifty in the next, sixty in the third year, seventy in the fourth. It can only add to the tax take: no updated return may declare a loss, shrink the liability, or enlarge a refund.

concepts.subsection: Section 40(b) — Partner remuneration limits
concepts.statement: A firm deducts working partners' remuneration only if the deed authorises it, and within the ceiling: on the first six lakh rupees of book profit (or a loss), the higher of three lakh rupees or ninety per cent of that slice; on the balance, sixty per cent — limits doubled by the Finance Act 2024 from assessment year 2025-26. Interest to partners caps at twelve per cent simple. From April 2025, section 194T adds ten per cent TDS on partner payments above twenty thousand rupees a year.

concepts.subsection: Section 36(1)(vii) — Bad debts
concepts.statement: A bad debt deducts in the year it is written off in the books — since 1989 the write-off itself is enough, and the assessee need not prove the debt actually became irrecoverable that year. The debt must have been counted in income earlier (or be money lent in a lending business). Recovery of an allowed bad debt is taxed when received, and a successor cannot claim the predecessor's debtor.

concepts.subsection: ICDS — Income computation and disclosure standards
concepts.statement: The ten notified ICDS govern computation of business income and other sources for taxpayers following mercantile accounting — they change the tax computation, never the books. Where ICDS diverges from accounting standards, ICDS wins for tax; where ICDS conflicts with the Act itself, the Act prevails. Familiar divergences: expected losses on construction contracts are not anticipated, marked-to-market losses are generally ignored, and retention money follows the ICDS timing.

concepts.subsection: Section 115BBC — Anonymous donations
concepts.statement: Donations for which a charitable trust maintains no record of the donor's name and address are taxed at thirty per cent — after a cushion of the higher of one lakh rupees or five per cent of total donations. Wholly religious institutions are outside the section entirely; mixed religious-charitable ones are caught only for donations directed to their educational or medical wings. The hundi at a temple and the box at a hospital answer to different rules.

concepts.subsection: Section 35D — Preliminary expenses
concepts.statement: Specified preliminary expenses — feasibility and project reports, engineering services, legal charges for agreements, and for companies the incorporation and issue expenses — amortise in five equal annual instalments from commencement or extension. The pool is capped at five per cent of the cost of the project (companies may take five per cent of capital employed instead); spending beyond the cap earns no deduction at all under the section.

concepts.subsection: First Schedule Part I — Clause 8
concepts.statement: Accepting an audit previously held by another chartered accountant without first communicating with him in writing is professional misconduct. The duty is to communicate — the outgoing auditor's permission or no-objection is not required, and the purpose is to learn whether the change hides something the incoming auditor should weigh.

concepts.subsection: Second Schedule Part I — Clause 1
concepts.statement: Disclosing information acquired in the course of a professional engagement to anyone other than the client, without the client's consent, is professional misconduct — unless law requires the disclosure. Legal compulsion and client consent are the only two doors out of the duty.

concepts.subsection: Second Schedule Part I — Clause 4
concepts.statement: Expressing an opinion on the financial statements of any business in which the member, his firm, or a partner in his firm has a substantial interest is professional misconduct. The clause reaches the firm and the partners, not only the signing member, and no disclosure cures it — the opinion itself is barred.

concepts.subsection: Second Schedule Part I — Clause 7
concepts.statement: Failing to exercise due diligence, or being grossly negligent in the conduct of professional duties, is professional misconduct. The clause needs no dishonesty and no client loss — signing what was never examined is the classic case.

concepts.subsection: First Schedule Part I — Clause 11
concepts.statement: A chartered accountant in practice may not engage in any business or occupation other than the profession unless the Council permits it. The clause's own proviso allows a directorship simpliciter — an ordinary board seat without managing or whole-time office — unless the member or a partner is interested in the company as its auditor. General and specific permissions of the Council carve the remaining space.

concepts.subsection: Second Schedule Part I — Clause 10
concepts.statement: Failing to keep a client's moneys — other than fees or money meant to be spent — in a separate banking account, or failing to use such moneys for their intended purpose within a reasonable time, is professional misconduct. The office account is for the firm's money; the client account is for the client's, and mixing them is the offence regardless of eventual repayment.

concepts.subsection: First Schedule Part I — Clause 7
concepts.statement: Advertising professional attainments or services, or using any designation other than chartered accountant on professional documents, cards or sign boards, is misconduct — a recognised university degree or a title indicating membership of an institute may be used. The Council's guidelines carve narrow permissions — write-ups within prescribed norms, websites on a pull basis — but self-praise pushed at the public stays barred.

concepts.subsection: First Schedule Part I — Clause 2
concepts.statement: Paying or allowing any share, commission or brokerage out of professional fees to anyone other than a member of the Institute, a partner, a retired partner, a deceased partner's legal representative, or a member of a permitted other professional body is misconduct. The clause polices the outflow of fees; referral commissions to clients, agents or relatives all fall on the wrong side.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Costs to obtain and fulfil a contract
concepts.statement: The incremental costs of obtaining a contract are recognised as an asset if the entity expects to recover them, with a practical expedient to expense them if the amortisation period is one year or less. Costs to fulfil a contract that are not within another Standard's scope are capitalised only if they relate directly to an identified contract, generate or enhance resources used to satisfy performance obligations, and are expected to be recovered.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Hedge accounting
concepts.statement: Hedge accounting is available only where the hedging relationship consists solely of eligible hedging instruments and eligible hedged items, there is formal designation and documentation at inception of the risk management objective and strategy, and the relationship meets the effectiveness requirements — an economic relationship between the hedged item and the hedging instrument, credit risk not dominating the value changes, and a hedge ratio consistent with actual risk management.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Derecognition of financial assets
concepts.statement: A financial asset is derecognised when the contractual rights to its cash flows expire, or when it is transferred and that transfer qualifies for derecognition — which turns on evaluating the extent to which the risks and rewards of ownership are retained. Substantially transferring risks and rewards derecognises the asset; substantially retaining them keeps it recognised in full, with a financial liability for the consideration received; only when neither is clear does the entity move on to a control test.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 12 — Deferred tax in a business combination
concepts.statement: Fair value adjustments to identifiable assets and liabilities recognised on a business combination create temporary differences whenever the tax base does not move to match, and the resulting deferred tax asset or liability is recognised as part of the acquisition accounting — increasing or decreasing goodwill or the bargain purchase gain. The one carve-out is goodwill itself — no deferred tax liability is recognised on its initial recognition, because that would only inflate goodwill further.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 21 — Net investment in a foreign operation
concepts.statement: Exchange differences on a monetary item that in substance forms part of an entity's net investment in a foreign operation are recognised in profit or loss in the separate or individual financial statements of the entity concerned, but in the financial statements that include the foreign operation — such as the group's consolidated statements — those exchange differences go to other comprehensive income and are reclassified to profit or loss only on disposal of the net investment.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 116 — Sale and leaseback
concepts.statement: In a sale and leaseback, the seller-lessee applies the Ind AS 115 requirements for identifying when a performance obligation is satisfied to judge whether the transfer is a sale. If it is, the seller-lessee measures the right-of-use asset retained at the proportion of the previous carrying amount relating to the rights retained, and recognises only the gain or loss relating to the rights transferred to the buyer-lessor — not the full gain on the asset. If the transfer fails the sale test, both parties account for it as a financing.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 36 — Timing of the goodwill impairment test
concepts.statement: A cash-generating unit to which goodwill has been allocated is tested for impairment at least annually, and the test may be performed at any time during the annual period provided it is performed at the same time every year; different units may be tested at different times. If some or all of the goodwill allocated to a unit was acquired in a business combination during the current period, that unit is tested before the end of the current annual period — the entity cannot wait for next year's cycle.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 33 — Diluted EPS and antidilution
concepts.statement: Diluted EPS adjusts profit and the weighted average number of shares for the effect of all dilutive potential equity shares, but a potential equity share that would increase EPS (or reduce a loss per share) is antidilutive and is excluded from the diluted EPS computation. Each issue or series of potential equity shares is tested for dilutive or antidilutive effect separately, not in aggregate.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 37 — Contingent assets
concepts.statement: A contingent asset is never recognised, because that could bring in income that may never be realised — but it is disclosed when an inflow of economic benefits is probable. Once realisation becomes virtually certain, the asset is no longer contingent and is recognised, together with the related income, in the period the change occurs.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 102 — Cash-settled share-based payment
concepts.statement: For a cash-settled share-based payment, the entity measures the goods or services received and the liability incurred at the fair value of the liability, and remeasures that fair value at the end of every reporting period and at settlement, with all changes recognised in profit or loss. Unlike an equity-settled award, the amount charged is never frozen at grant date — it moves with the liability's fair value until the award is paid.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 1 — Going concern disclosure
concepts.statement: Management assesses the entity's ability to continue as a going concern, looking at least twelve months from the reporting date, and prepares the financial statements on that basis unless it intends to liquidate or cease trading or has no realistic alternative. Where management identifies material uncertainties that cast significant doubt on that ability, those uncertainties are disclosed — disclosure, not abandonment of the going concern basis, is the standard's response short of an actual intention to liquidate.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 8 — Correction of prior period errors
concepts.statement: A material prior period error is corrected retrospectively in the first financial statements approved after its discovery, by restating the comparative amounts for the period the error occurred, or restating opening balances if the error predates the earliest period presented. The correction bypasses profit or loss for the period of discovery — it adjusts the periods actually affected, not the current period's result.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 103 Appendix C — Combinations under common control
concepts.statement: IFRS 3 pushes combinations of entities under common control out of its scope; Ind AS 103 pulls them back in through Appendix C and answers them with the pooling of interests method. Assets and liabilities come across at their existing carrying amounts, no fair values are recognised and no new goodwill arises, the only adjustments permitted are to harmonise accounting policies, prior period figures are restated as if the combination had happened from the beginning of the preceding period, the transferor's reserves keep their identity, and the difference between the consideration and the transferor's share capital is put to capital reserve.

citation.ref: Appendix C, para 8, para 9 and para 12

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 103 — Contingent consideration after the acquisition
concepts.statement: How contingent consideration moves after the acquisition date is decided by how it was classified on that date. Classified as equity, it is never remeasured and its settlement is accounted for within equity. Classified as an asset or a liability within the scope of Ind AS 109, it is remeasured to fair value at every reporting date with the change in profit or loss. Only a change that reflects new information about facts existing at the acquisition date is a measurement period adjustment that touches goodwill; a change caused by the acquiree's later performance never does.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Ownership change without loss of control
concepts.statement: Once control exists, buying more of a subsidiary or selling part of it without losing control is a transaction with owners in their capacity as owners, not an acquisition or a disposal. The carrying amounts of the controlling and non-controlling interests are adjusted to their new relative shares, and any difference between that adjustment and the fair value of the consideration paid or received is recognised directly in equity and attributed to the owners of the parent. No goodwill is created or released, and nothing reaches profit or loss.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Reclassifying financial assets
concepts.statement: Financial assets are reclassified when, and only when, the entity changes the business model for managing them. Financial liabilities are never reclassified. The change bites on the reclassification date, which the Standard defines as the first day of the first reporting period following the change of business model, so measurement carries on unchanged until the period ends. From that date the new classification applies prospectively, and previously recognised interest, gains and losses are not restated.

citation.ref: para 4.4.1 and 5.6.1, with the Appendix A definition of reclassification date

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Modifying a financial liability
concepts.statement: Renegotiating a borrowing is tested before it is accounted for. Terms are substantially different if the present value of the cash flows under the new terms, including fees paid net of fees received and discounted at the original effective interest rate, differs by at least 10 per cent from the present value of the remaining cash flows of the old liability. Substantially different means the old liability is extinguished and a new one recognised, with the difference between the old carrying amount and the consideration paid taken to profit or loss. Below the threshold, the liability survives and only its carrying amount is recomputed.

citation.ref: para 3.3.2 and 3.3.3, with the 10 per cent test in para B3.3.6

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Significant financing component
concepts.statement: Where the timing of payments gives either the customer or the entity a significant benefit of financing the transfer of goods or services, the promised consideration is adjusted for the time value of money, so that revenue is recognised at the amount the customer would have paid in cash on the date of transfer. It works in both directions, a long advance as much as long credit. A practical expedient excuses the adjustment where the gap between transfer and payment is expected at inception to be one year or less. The discount rate is the one implicit in a separate financing transaction between the two parties at inception, and it is never updated afterwards.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 116 — Lessee accounting for a lease modification
concepts.statement: A lessee treats a modification as a separate lease only when both gates open, the scope increases by adding the right to use one or more underlying assets and the consideration goes up by an amount commensurate with the stand-alone price for that increase. Otherwise the lessee reallocates the consideration, redetermines the lease term, and remeasures the lease liability at a revised discount rate. Where the modification decreases the scope, the right-of-use asset is first cut back to reflect the partial or full termination and the resulting gain or loss goes to profit or loss; for every other modification the whole remeasurement is absorbed by the right-of-use asset.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 12 — Deferred tax on investments in subsidiaries and associates
concepts.statement: Undistributed profits of a subsidiary, branch, associate or joint arrangement create a taxable temporary difference between the carrying amount of the investment in the consolidated financial statements and its tax base. A deferred tax liability is recognised on all of them except where both conditions hold together, the investor can control the timing of the reversal and it is probable the difference will not reverse in the foreseeable future. A parent controls its subsidiary's dividend policy and can meet both; an investor in an associate cannot control that policy, so the exception is rarely available there.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 36 — Allocating an impairment loss within a unit
concepts.statement: An impairment loss on a cash-generating unit is allocated in a fixed order, first against any goodwill allocated to the unit until that goodwill is nil, and only then across the unit's other assets pro rata on their carrying amounts. No individual asset may be written below the highest of its own fair value less costs of disposal where measurable, its value in use where determinable, and zero; whatever the floor blocks is reallocated pro rata to the remaining assets. Goodwill written off this way can never be reversed in a later period, even if the unit recovers.

citation.ref: para 104 and 105, with the reversal bar in para 124

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 113 — Principal market and the price used
concepts.statement: Fair value is measured in the principal market, the market with the greatest volume and level of activity that the entity can access, and only where no principal market exists does the most advantageous market answer. Where a principal market exists, its price is used even if a different market would net the entity more. That price is not adjusted for transaction costs, which are specific to a transaction rather than a characteristic of the asset, but it is adjusted for transport costs where location is a characteristic of the asset.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 105 — Presenting a discontinued operation
concepts.statement: A discontinued operation is a component disposed of or classified as held for sale that is a separate major line of business or geographical area, part of a single coordinated plan to dispose of one, or a subsidiary acquired exclusively for resale. Its post-tax result and the post-tax gain or loss on measurement or disposal are collapsed into a single amount in the statement of profit and loss, with the analysis given in the notes. The profit or loss figures for prior periods are re-presented on the same basis; the balance sheets of prior periods are expressly left alone.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 19 — Past service cost
concepts.statement: Past service cost is the change in the present value of the defined benefit obligation caused by a plan amendment or a curtailment. It is recognised as an expense in full at the earlier of the date the amendment or curtailment occurs and the date the entity recognises related restructuring costs or termination benefits. There is no spreading over a vesting period and no distinction between vested and unvested benefits, and past service cost is part of service cost in profit or loss, not a remeasurement in other comprehensive income.

citation.ref: para 102 and 103, with the components in para 120

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Attributing results to non-controlling interests
concepts.statement: Profit or loss and each component of other comprehensive income are attributed to the owners of the parent and to the non-controlling interests, and total comprehensive income is attributed to both even where this leaves the non-controlling interests with a deficit balance — there is no floor at nil, unlike the equity method for an associate. Where a subsidiary has cumulative preference shares classified as equity and held by non-controlling interests, the group computes its share only after adjusting for the dividends on those shares, whether or not they have been declared.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — The investment entity exception
concepts.statement: An investment entity is one that takes funds from investors to provide them with investment management services, commits to invest solely for capital appreciation or investment income, and measures performance on a fair value basis. It does not consolidate its subsidiaries and does not apply Ind AS 103 on obtaining control; it measures each investment in a subsidiary at fair value through profit or loss. The one carve-out is a subsidiary providing services relating to the investment entity's own investment activities, which is consolidated. A parent that is not itself an investment entity consolidates everything it controls, including what it controls through an investment entity subsidiary.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 28 — Upstream and downstream transactions with an associate
concepts.statement: Gains and losses on sales between an investor and its associate or joint venture are recognised only to the extent of unrelated investors' interests, so the investor's own percentage of the unrealised profit is eliminated and no more. A downstream sale reduces the investor's own profit by its share; an upstream sale reduces its share of the associate's profit. Elimination is never in full, which is where an associate parts company with a consolidated subsidiary. Where the transaction evidences a fall in net realisable value or an impairment, that loss is recognised in full on a downstream sale.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 111 — Acquiring an interest in a joint operation that is a business
concepts.statement: Where the activity of a joint operation constitutes a business, an entity acquiring an interest in it applies, to the extent of its share, all the Ind AS 103 business combination principles that do not conflict with Ind AS 111 — identifiable assets and liabilities at fair value, acquisition-related costs expensed, goodwill recognised and tested annually. This holds for an additional interest as much as the first. The departure from a step acquisition is that previously held interests are not remeasured where the joint operator retains joint control.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 21 — Translating a foreign operation into the presentation currency
concepts.statement: To carry a foreign operation into a different presentation currency, assets and liabilities for every balance sheet presented go at the closing rate at that balance sheet date, income and expenses go at the exchange rates at the dates of the transactions with an average rate accepted as an approximation, and all resulting exchange differences go to other comprehensive income. Those differences come from two sources, retranslating the opening net assets at a new closing rate and translating the result at a rate that is not the closing rate, and they accumulate in a separate component of equity until disposal.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Measuring a cash flow hedge
concepts.statement: The cash flow hedge reserve is adjusted to the lower, in absolute amounts, of the cumulative gain or loss on the hedging instrument and the cumulative change in the present value of the hedged expected future cash flows, both from inception. That effective portion goes to other comprehensive income and everything left over is hedge ineffectiveness in profit or loss. If the hedged forecast transaction later produces a non-financial asset or liability, the accumulated reserve is removed and included directly in that item's initial cost, which is not a reclassification adjustment; in every other case it is reclassified to profit or loss in the periods the hedged cash flows affect profit or loss.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — The general expected credit loss model
concepts.statement: Outside the simplified approach, a loss allowance is measured at 12-month expected credit losses unless credit risk has increased significantly since initial recognition, when it moves to lifetime expected credit losses. The test compares the risk of a default occurring at the reporting date with that risk at initial recognition, not the change in the amount of the losses. Two shortcuts sit either side of it — an entity may assume no significant increase where the instrument has low credit risk at the reporting date, and there is a rebuttable presumption of a significant increase once contractual payments are more than 30 days past due.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 37 — Measuring a provision
concepts.statement: A provision is the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the end of the reporting period. Where a large population of items is involved the estimate is the expected value, weighting all possible outcomes by their probabilities; where a single obligation is involved the most likely outcome may be the best estimate. Discounting is required only where the effect of the time value of money is material, at a pre-tax rate reflecting current market assessments and the risks specific to the liability. A reimbursement is recognised only when it is virtually certain, as a separate asset capped at the provision, and may be netted only in the statement of profit and loss.

citation.ref: para 36, 39, 45, 47 and 53, with the presentation in para 54

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 20 — Repaying a government grant
concepts.statement: A government grant that becomes repayable is a change in accounting estimate, never a prior period error. Repayment of a grant related to income is applied first against any unamortised deferred credit, with the excess straight to profit or loss. Repayment of a grant related to an asset is recognised by increasing the carrying amount of the asset or reducing the deferred income balance, and the cumulative additional depreciation that would have been charged in the absence of the grant goes immediately to profit or loss. The pre-2018 Indian text allowed only the deferred income route and carried no depreciation catch-up.

citation.ref: para 32 as substituted in 2018, with para 33

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 41 — Government grants for biological assets
concepts.statement: Ind AS 41 deliberately departs from Ind AS 20 for a biological asset measured at fair value less costs to sell. An unconditional grant on such an asset goes to profit or loss when, and only when, it becomes receivable — not when it is received and not spread over anything. A conditional grant goes to profit or loss when, and only when, the conditions are met, with time-apportionment allowed only where the terms let part of the grant be retained as time passes. Ind AS 20 returns only where the biological asset is measured at cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment.

citation.ref: para 34, 35 and 36, with the scope split in para 37 and 38

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 Appendix C — Service concession arrangements
concepts.statement: Infrastructure inside a public-to-private service concession is never the operator's property, plant and equipment, because the arrangement does not convey the right to control its use. The operator is a service provider, and what it books for construction depends on what the grantor gives back. An unconditional contractual right to receive cash from the grantor produces a financial asset; a right, or licence, to charge users of the public service produces an intangible asset, because those amounts turn on how much the public uses the service. That split also decides borrowing costs — expensed under the financial asset model, capitalised during construction under the intangible asset model.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 23 — Capitalisation rate on general borrowings
concepts.statement: Funds borrowed specifically for a qualifying asset yield the actual borrowing costs incurred on that borrowing less any investment income on the temporary investment of those borrowings. Funds borrowed generally yield a capitalisation rate applied to the expenditure on the asset, the rate being the weighted average of the borrowing costs on the entity's borrowings outstanding during the period other than those made specifically for a qualifying asset. Whatever the two limbs produce, the amount capitalised in a period can never exceed the borrowing costs actually incurred in that period.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 33 — Rights issue and the bonus element
concepts.statement: A rights issue priced below fair value is part fresh money and part gift, and only the gift is retrospective. The shares outstanding before the issue are multiplied by the fair value per share immediately before the exercise of rights over the theoretical ex-rights fair value per share, that theoretical price being the aggregate fair value of the existing shares plus the proceeds of the rights, divided by the shares outstanding after the exercise. The adjusted number is used for all periods before the rights issue, so the comparative earnings per share is restated, while the new shares themselves enter the weighted average from their own date.

citation.ref: para 27(b), with Appendix A, para A2

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 34 — Income tax in an interim period
concepts.statement: Interim income tax expense is recognised on the best estimate of the weighted average annual income tax rate expected for the full financial year, applied to the year-to-date profit. When the estimate of that annual rate changes, the amount accrued in an earlier interim period of the same financial year is adjusted through the later interim period, so the catch-up lands in the current quarter. Amounts reported in earlier interim periods are not retrospectively adjusted, and no interim period is measured as though it stood alone.

citation.ref: para 30(c), read with para 28 and para 36

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 108 — Entity-wide disclosures
concepts.statement: Three disclosures bind every entity within Ind AS 108, including one with a single reportable segment, and are given only where the segment note has not already given them. Revenues from external customers by product or service; revenues and non-current assets other than financial instruments, deferred tax assets, post-employment benefit assets and insurance rights, split between the country of domicile and all foreign countries in total with any material individual country shown separately; and the fact of any single external customer at 10 per cent or more of revenues, with the amount and the reporting segment but not the customer's name.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 102 — Modifying and cancelling an equity-settled award
concepts.statement: Whatever is done to an equity-settled award afterwards, the entity recognises as a minimum the services received at the grant date fair value of the instruments granted, unless they fail a vesting condition other than a market condition. On top of that it recognises the effects of modifications that increase the total fair value or are otherwise beneficial to the employee. The incremental fair value is the difference between the modified and the original instrument, both measured at the modification date, spread from that date to vesting. A modification that reduces fair value is ignored, and a cancellation or settlement during the vesting period is an acceleration of vesting.

citation.ref: para 27 and 28, with Appendix B, para B43 and B44

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.statement: Revenue is recognised when (or as) a performance obligation is satisfied by transferring control of the promised good or service to the customer. Transfer of control, not transfer of risks and rewards, is the recognition trigger.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 2 — Inventories
concepts.statement: Inventories of items that are not ordinarily interchangeable are costed by specific identification. For the rest, FIFO or weighted average is used. LIFO is not permitted.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Consolidated Financial Statements
concepts.statement: An investor controls an investee only when it has all three elements together — power over the investee, exposure or rights to variable returns, and the ability to use its power to affect those returns. Control does not require a majority shareholding.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Financial Instruments
concepts.statement: Loss allowances are measured on an expected credit loss basis, recognised from initial recognition without waiting for a default. For trade receivables the simplified approach applies, and the allowance is always lifetime expected credit losses.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 103 — Business Combinations
concepts.statement: Under the Indian carve-out, a gain on a bargain purchase is recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in capital reserve, not in profit or loss — unlike IFRS 3, which takes it to profit or loss.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.statement: A performance obligation is satisfied over time only when one of three criteria is met — the customer consumes the benefit as the entity performs, the customer controls the asset as it is created, or the asset has no alternative use and the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance to date. Otherwise control passes at a point in time.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 37 — Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
concepts.statement: A provision is recognised only when all three conditions hold — a present obligation, legal or constructive, from a past event; a probable outflow of resources; and a reliable estimate. For a restructuring, the obligating event is announcing the plan to those affected or beginning to implement it, never the board decision alone.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 16 — Property, Plant and Equipment
concepts.statement: The cost of a major inspection or overhaul that is a condition of continuing to operate an asset is capitalised into the asset's carrying amount when incurred, and any remaining carrying amount of the previous inspection is derecognised — even if the previous inspection's cost was never separately identified.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 21 — The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
concepts.statement: At each reporting date, foreign currency monetary items are translated at the closing rate, with exchange differences to profit or loss. Non-monetary items carried at historical cost stay at the transaction-date rate. Whether an item is money fixes which rate it gets.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 38 — Intangible Assets
concepts.statement: Internally generated goodwill is never recognised as an asset, and internally generated brands, mastheads, customer lists and similar items are barred with it. Development costs are the exception, capitalised only from the day all six conditions are demonstrated; research is always expensed.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 108 — Operating Segments
concepts.statement: An operating segment is separately reportable if it crosses ten per cent of combined revenue (internal plus external), of the greater of combined profits or combined losses, or of combined assets — and reportable segments must together cover seventy-five per cent of external revenue, adding segments until they do.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 1 — Presentation of Financial Statements
concepts.statement: A liability is current when the entity lacks, at the reporting date, the right to defer settlement for at least twelve months. A covenant breached by the year end makes the loan payable on demand and therefore current — unless the lender agreed, on or before the reporting date, not to demand payment; a waiver arriving after the year end comes too late to change the classification.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 7 — Statement of Cash Flows
concepts.statement: Under the Indian carve-out, an entity other than a financial institution classifies interest paid as a financing cash flow and interest and dividends received as investing — the options IFRS offers are removed. A bank classifies all of them as operating, because lending is its business.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 116 — Leases
concepts.statement: A lessee recognises a right-of-use asset and a lease liability for every lease, with two elections out — leases of twelve months or less with no purchase option, and leases of low-value assets. The exemptions are elections about recognition, not about whether the contract is a lease.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 36 — Impairment of Assets
concepts.statement: An asset is impaired when its carrying amount exceeds its recoverable amount, and recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use. Higher — the entity keeps the better of selling and using, so either measure alone can clear the asset of impairment.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 10 — Events after the Reporting Period
concepts.statement: An event after the reporting period adjusts the financial statements only when it evidences a condition that existed at the reporting date; a condition that arose afterwards is disclosed, not adjusted. Dividends declared after the reporting period are the standard's own worked example — no liability at the reporting date, however certain the declaration.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 105 — Non-current Assets Held for Sale
concepts.statement: Held-for-sale classification needs the asset available for immediate sale in its present condition and the sale highly probable — management committed to a plan, an active programme to find a buyer, active marketing at a reasonable price, and completion expected within a year. Once classified, the asset is measured at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell, and depreciation stops.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 8 — Policies, Estimates and Errors
concepts.statement: A change in accounting policy is applied retrospectively, restating comparatives as if the new policy had always applied; a change in accounting estimate is recognised prospectively, in the period of change and the future. Where the two are hard to tell apart, the standard itself says treat the change as an estimate. Depreciation method and useful life are estimates; measurement basis is policy.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 23 — Borrowing Costs
concepts.statement: Borrowing costs directly attributable to acquiring, constructing or producing a qualifying asset — one that necessarily takes a substantial period to get ready for its intended use or sale — are capitalised as part of the asset's cost; all other borrowing costs are expensed. Capitalisation is suspended during extended periods when active development pauses, and ends when the asset is substantially ready.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 40 — Investment Property
concepts.statement: Ind AS 40 permits only the cost model for investment property — the Indian carve-out removed IAS 40's fair value model. Fair value is still measured and disclosed in the notes, but the balance sheet carries cost less depreciation and impairment. Property held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation, not for use in production or administration, is what the standard covers.

citation.ref: measurement after recognition (cost model; fair value model not permitted)

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 113 — Fair Value Measurement
concepts.statement: The fair value hierarchy ranks inputs, not techniques: Level 1 is unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical items; Level 2 is other observable inputs — quoted prices for similar items, or corroborated market data; Level 3 is unobservable inputs. A measurement sits at the lowest level of any input significant to it, and Level 1 prices are used unadjusted where available.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 102 — Share-based Payment
concepts.statement: For equity-settled awards to employees, the expense is measured at the fair value of the equity instruments at grant date — and that value is never remeasured, however the share price moves. What does move is the number of awards expected to vest under service and non-market conditions, trued up each period until vesting. Market conditions are priced into grant-date value once and never trued up.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 19 — Employee Benefits
concepts.statement: Defined benefit cost splits three ways: service cost and net interest go to profit or loss; remeasurements — actuarial gains and losses, and the return on plan assets beyond the amount already in net interest — go to other comprehensive income, and once there they are never reclassified to profit or loss. The split keeps the operating result clear of actuarial volatility without hiding it.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 28 — Investments in Associates
concepts.statement: Twenty per cent or more of voting power presumes significant influence — the power to participate in financial and operating policy decisions — and less than twenty presumes its absence; both presumptions yield to clear demonstration otherwise. Board representation, policy participation, material transactions, interchange of personnel or essential technical dependence can evidence influence below the line. An associate is equity accounted, not consolidated.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 12 — Income Taxes
concepts.statement: A deferred tax asset on unused tax losses is recognised only to the extent future taxable profit is probable — and a history of recent losses is itself evidence against that. A loss-making entity records the asset only to the extent of taxable temporary differences or convincing other evidence of future profit, such as a firm order book from a cause that has demonstrably ended.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Classification of financial assets
concepts.statement: A financial asset is carried at amortised cost only when both tests pass: the business model is to hold and collect contractual cash flows, and those cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest. Held-to-collect with equity-linked returns fails the second; plain-interest bonds bought for trading fail the first. Failures land in fair value categories.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 103 — Non-controlling interest at acquisition
concepts.statement: For each business combination, the acquirer measures qualifying non-controlling interest at either full fair value or the proportionate share of the acquiree's identifiable net assets — a choice made combination by combination, not as a standing policy. The choice sets goodwill: fair value NCI produces full goodwill including the minority's share; the proportionate route recognises only the acquirer's goodwill.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 116 — Lessor accounting
concepts.statement: Lessors still classify: a lease that transfers substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership is a finance lease — derecognise the asset, recognise a receivable; otherwise it is an operating lease — keep the asset, book income over the term. Indicators include ownership transfer, a bargain purchase option, the term covering the major part of economic life, and present value of payments amounting to substantially all the fair value. Lessee accounting became single-model; lessor accounting did not.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 32 — Liability or equity
concepts.statement: An instrument is classified by substance against the definitions, not by its legal name: a contractual obligation to deliver cash — mandatory redemption, compulsory dividends — makes a financial liability, however the instrument is titled. Preference shares redeemable at the holder's option or on a fixed date are debt; pure discretion over both dividends and redemption keeps an instrument in equity. Classification happens once, at issue.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 33 — EPS and bonus issues
concepts.statement: A bonus issue, split or similar event changes the share count without changing resources, so EPS treats the new count as if it had existed from the beginning of the earliest period presented — restating the comparative EPS too. A fresh issue for cash, by contrast, enters the weighted average only from its date, because new resources arrived then.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 24 — Related Party Disclosures
concepts.statement: Key management personnel compensation is disclosed in total and by category — short-term, post-employment, other long-term, termination, share-based. Related party disclosure is about relationships and transactions, not approval: arm's length terms may be claimed only if they can be substantiated, and a government-related entity gets a partial exemption for dealings with its government and its sister entities, disclosing the nature and extent instead of every transaction.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 34 — Interim Financial Reporting
concepts.statement: Interim statements apply the same accounting policies as the annual ones — a quarter is not a licence for different measurement — and reporting frequency must not change the annual result: measurements run year-to-date, so a third-quarter estimate correction adjusts the year-to-date figures rather than fabricating a standalone quarter. Costs that fail asset definitions at year-end fail them equally at a quarter's end.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 37 — Onerous contracts
concepts.statement: A contract whose unavoidable costs of fulfilment exceed the benefits expected under it is onerous, and the present obligation is provided for at once — the unavoidable cost being the lower of the cost of fulfilling and the penalty of exiting. Routine cancellable purchase orders create no obligation, and expected future operating losses of the business generally are never provided for; the onerous contract is the exception because the loss is contracted, not merely forecast.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 111 — Joint operations and joint ventures
concepts.statement: Joint control is contractually agreed sharing of control where the relevant decisions need unanimous consent. The arrangement's type decides the accounting: joint operators have rights to the assets and obligations for the liabilities and record their share of each, line by line; joint venturers have rights only to the net assets and equity-account the investment. Structure through a separate vehicle starts, not ends, the classification.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 20 — Government grants
concepts.statement: A government grant is recognised only when there is reasonable assurance the entity will comply with its conditions and the grant will be received. Since the 2018 amendment, a grant related to an asset may be presented either as deferred income released over the asset's life, or by deducting it from the asset's carrying amount — the pre-2018 Indian text had removed the deduction option, and stale materials still teach that removal.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 101 — First-time adoption
concepts.statement: A first-time adopter may elect deemed cost for property, plant and equipment at the transition date: fair value at that date, or the previous GAAP carrying amount where eligible — instead of rebuilding depreciated cost as if Ind AS had always applied. The elections are optional exemptions from full retrospective application; the general rule remains retrospective, and mandatory exceptions forbid hindsight in estimates.

citation.ref: deemed cost exemption for PPE at transition

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Principal versus agent
concepts.statement: An entity is a principal when it controls the promised good or service before transfer to the customer, reporting gross revenue; an agent arranges for another to provide it, reporting only its fee or commission. Momentary legal title on the way through does not make a principal; inventory risk, primary responsibility for fulfilment and discretion in setting prices indicate control. The revenue difference is presentation, not profit.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Loss of control
concepts.statement: When a parent loses control of a subsidiary it derecognises the subsidiary's assets, liabilities and NCI, recognises the consideration received, and measures any retained interest at fair value at that date — that fair value becomes the cost of the new associate or investment. The gain or loss in profit or loss thus includes a remeasurement of the stake kept, not only the stake sold; control is an all-or-nothing line.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 16 — Revaluation model
concepts.statement: Under the revaluation model an upward revaluation goes to other comprehensive income and accumulates in equity as revaluation surplus — except to the extent it reverses a decrease earlier charged to profit or loss. A downward revaluation charges profit or loss — except to the extent a surplus for that same asset exists to absorb it. The surplus never passes through profit or loss: on disposal it transfers directly to retained earnings.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 2 — NRV and the raw materials exception
concepts.statement: Inventories are carried at the lower of cost and net realisable value, item by item — but raw materials are not written down below cost while the finished products they will enter are expected to sell at or above cost. Only when the materials' price decline signals that the finished product's cost exceeds its NRV do the materials write down, with replacement cost as their best available measure.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 41 — Agriculture
concepts.statement: Biological assets are measured at each reporting date at fair value less costs to sell, with changes through profit or loss — cost models yield to the market's verdict on living, growing assets. Bearer plants — the tea bush, not the tea leaf — are carved out to Ind AS 16 as plant-like assets, while the produce growing on them stays in Ind AS 41 until harvest, when it moves to Ind AS 2 at its harvest-date fair value as deemed cost.

concepts.subsection: Schedule III — Mandated ratios and disclosures
concepts.statement: Division II of Schedule III requires eleven named ratios in the notes — current ratio, debt-equity, debt service coverage, return on equity, inventory and receivables and payables turnover, net capital turnover, net profit, return on capital employed, return on investment — with the elements of each computation and an explanation wherever a ratio moved more than twenty-five per cent from the prior year. The amendments also demand disclosure of benami proceedings, undisclosed income surrendered, and crypto holdings.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 28 — Sharing an associate's losses
concepts.statement: Equity accounting absorbs an associate's losses only down to zero: once the investor's share of losses equals its interest — the equity-method carrying amount plus long-term interests that are in substance part of the net investment — recognition of further losses stops, resuming only after future profits rebuild the base. Losses beyond zero are provided only where the investor has legal or constructive obligations or made payments for the associate.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Constraining variable consideration
concepts.statement: Variable consideration — bonuses, penalties, volume rebates, royalties — enters the transaction price only to the extent it is highly probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue will not occur when the uncertainty resolves. Estimation uses the expected value or the most likely amount, whichever predicts better; the constraint then trims the estimate. Booking the hopeful number and reversing later is the pattern the rule exists to stop.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 7 — Cash and cash equivalents
concepts.statement: Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments readily convertible to known amounts of cash with insignificant risk of value change — normally maturing within about three months of acquisition. Equity investments are excluded save in-substance equivalents. Bank overdrafts repayable on demand that form an integral part of cash management join cash and cash equivalents, turning the statement's bottom line negative-capable.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Consolidation procedures
concepts.statement: Consolidation combines like items line by line, eliminates the parent's investment against its share of each subsidiary's equity, and eliminates intragroup balances, transactions and unrealised profits in full — not merely the parent's share. The group reports as one economic entity under uniform accounting policies for like transactions, restating a subsidiary's numbers where its policies differ.

concepts.subsection: Board meeting quorum — section 174
concepts.statement: Quorum for a board meeting is the higher of one-third of the total strength of directors (any fraction rounded up) or two directors. A director interested in an item under section 184(2) is left out of the count for that item, and telephonic assent from a director not participating by the prescribed video-conferencing means does not count as presence. Absent quorum, the meeting stands automatically adjourned to the same day the following week, same time and place, unless the articles say otherwise.

concepts.subsection: Frequency of board meetings — section 173
concepts.statement: Every company holds at least four board meetings a year, with the gap between two consecutive meetings never exceeding one hundred and twenty days, and the first meeting within thirty days of incorporation. A one person company, small company, dormant company or private start-up needs only one meeting in each half of the calendar year, with a minimum gap of ninety days between the two — a relaxation, not the general rule.

concepts.subsection: Board powers needing shareholder approval — section 180
concepts.statement: The board cannot, by its own resolution, sell, lease or otherwise dispose of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking, or borrow beyond the aggregate of paid-up capital, free reserves and securities premium (ordinary-course temporary bank loans excepted) — both need a special resolution of the shareholders first, obtained before the act, not disclosed to them after it.

concepts.subsection: Retirement by rotation — section 152
concepts.statement: Independent directors are never liable to retire by rotation. Of the remaining directors of a public company, at least two-thirds must be liable to rotation, of which one-third (or the number nearest to one-third) retires at every annual general meeting, the director longest in office retiring first and being eligible for reappointment. Articles cannot exempt directors from rotation below this statutory floor.

concepts.subsection: Disclosure of directors' interest — section 184
concepts.statement: Every director discloses his concern or interest in any company, body corporate, firm or association of individuals at the first board meeting he attends in a financial year, and again on any change — a duty owed regardless of the size of the interest. Separately, an interested director discloses that interest in a specific contract or arrangement and does not participate in the board's discussion or vote on it; a contract entered in breach is voidable at the company's option.

concepts.subsection: Contract of employment with managing or whole-time director — section 190
concepts.statement: A company keeps at its registered office a copy of its managing or whole-time director's contract of service, or a written memorandum of its terms where the contract is not in writing, open for inspection by members without charge during business hours — a members' right the board or the company secretary cannot narrow to itself or to the auditor.

concepts.subsection: Consolidated financial statements — section 129(3)
concepts.statement: A company with one or more subsidiaries, including associate companies and joint ventures, prepares a consolidated financial statement in addition to its standalone statements, in the same form and manner, following the applicable accounting standards, and lays it before the annual general meeting alongside the standalone statements. Consolidation covers every subsidiary; it is not a management choice of which ones to fold in.

concepts.subsection: Board's report contents — section 134
concepts.statement: The board's report states, among other prescribed particulars, a director's responsibility statement under section 134(5), particulars of loans, guarantees and investments under section 186, particulars of related-party contracts in the prescribed form, the CSR policy and initiatives, and — for listed and other prescribed companies — a statement on the formal annual evaluation of the board, its committees and individual directors. These are matters the report must itself state, not particulars merely available on request.

concepts.subsection: Annual return and its certification — section 92
concepts.statement: Every company files its annual return with the Registrar within sixty days of the annual general meeting, or of the date by which the AGM should have been held where none took place, in which case a statement of the reasons for the default goes with it. Section 92(2) leaves the size line to the rules, and Rule 11(2) draws it at a listed company, or a company with paid-up share capital of ₹10 crore or more, or turnover of ₹50 crore or more: such a return must additionally be certified by a company secretary in practice in Form MGT-8. The two size tests are alternatives — crossing either is enough — and listing is a third, independent route in.

citation.ref: Sections 92(2) and 92(4), read with Rule 11(2) of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014 (Form MGT-8)

concepts.subsection: Rights issue procedure — section 62
concepts.statement: A rights issue offer goes to existing equity shareholders in proportion to their holding, stays open for not less than fifteen days and not more than thirty days, and carries a right of renunciation in favour of another person unless the articles exclude it. The board cannot allot before the offer period lapses or ahead of renunciation choices being exercised or declined.

concepts.subsection: Debentures — trustee and redemption reserve, section 71
concepts.statement: Section 71(5) stops a company from issuing a prospectus, or making an offer or invitation to the public or to more than five hundred of its members, for subscription of its debentures unless it has appointed one or more debenture trustees before that issue or offer. What pulls the trustee in is the kind of offer, not the size of the borrowing — the section names no rupee figure at all. Rule 18(1)(c) adds that the trustee comes before the prospectus or letter of offer goes out, and the debenture trust deed is executed within sixty days of allotment, so an independent party holds the security and enforces the debenture-holders' rights; the issuer's own guarantee is not a substitute for that office. Section 71(4) separately requires a debenture redemption reserve out of profits available for dividend, but Rule 18(7) as it now stands excuses listed companies, NBFCs registered under section 45-IA of the RBI Act and housing finance companies registered with the National Housing Bank; other unlisted companies keep a reserve of ten per cent of the outstanding value of the debentures.

citation.ref: Sections 71(4) and 71(5), read with Rules 18(1)(c) and 18(7) of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014

concepts.subsection: Moratorium under the IBC — section 14
concepts.statement: On admission of a corporate insolvency resolution application, the adjudicating authority declares a moratorium barring institution or continuation of suits against the corporate debtor, transfer or disposal of its assets, enforcement of any security interest, and recovery of property by an owner or lessor in the debtor's possession; supply of essential goods and services to the debtor cannot be terminated during this period. The moratorium does not extend to a surety in a contract of guarantee for the corporate debtor.

concepts.subsection: CIRP time limit — section 12 of the IBC
concepts.statement: A corporate insolvency resolution process must be completed within one hundred and eighty days of the insolvency commencement date. The committee of creditors may resolve, by a vote of sixty-six per cent of voting share under section 12(2), to instruct the resolution professional to seek one extension of up to ninety days — one only, never a second. The proviso to section 12(3) then caps the whole process at three hundred and thirty days from the insolvency commencement date, and that outer figure expressly swallows the time taken in legal proceedings relating to the process. The Supreme Court in Essar Steel read down the word "mandatorily" so a tribunal may go past three hundred and thirty days in an exceptional case where the delay is the tribunal's own, but that is a rescue, not the rule.

citation.ref: Sections 12(1), 12(2) and the proviso to section 12(3), as inserted by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2019

concepts.subsection: Committee of creditors — related parties and voting thresholds
concepts.statement: The committee of creditors comprises all financial creditors of the corporate debtor, but the first proviso to section 21(2) strips a financial creditor that is a related party of the corporate debtor of any right of representation, participation or voting in the committee. Losing the vote is not losing the claim — the related party remains a financial creditor whose debt is admitted and paid in its class. The committee's ordinary decisions need fifty-one per cent of voting share under section 21(8); the actions listed in section 28(1) need sixty-six per cent under section 28(3), and so does approval of a resolution plan under section 30(4). "Related party" here is the IBC's own definition in section 5(24), which is wider than section 2(76) of the Companies Act — and the corporate debtor's related-party disclosure under Ind AS 24 continues through the process regardless of who may vote.

concepts.subsection: Liquidation waterfall — section 53 of the IBC
concepts.statement: Section 53(1) distributes liquidation proceeds in a fixed order that overrides anything to the contrary in any other law - (a) insolvency resolution process costs and liquidation costs in full; (b) workmen's dues for the twenty-four months preceding the liquidation commencement date and debts owed to a secured creditor who has relinquished its security, ranking equally between themselves; (c) wages and unpaid dues of employees other than workmen for the twelve months preceding that date; (d) financial debts owed to unsecured creditors; (e) government dues for the two years preceding that date and any amount left unpaid to a secured creditor that enforced its own security, ranking equally; (f) any remaining debts and dues; (g) preference shareholders; (h) equity shareholders or partners. Section 327(7) of the Companies Act, 2013 shuts sections 326 and 327 — the Companies Act's own preferential payments — out of a liquidation under the Code, and the Supreme Court upheld that exclusion in Moser Baer Karamchari Union.

citation.ref: Section 53(1), read with section 327(7) of the Companies Act, 2013

concepts.subsection: Ineligible resolution applicant — section 29A and the MSME relaxation
concepts.statement: Section 29A lists the persons who may not submit a resolution plan, and section 30(4) obliges the committee of creditors to check eligibility before approving one. Clause (c) catches a person whose account, or an account of a corporate debtor under his management, has been classified as a non-performing asset with at least one year gone from that classification to the insolvency commencement date. Clause (h) catches a person who has executed a guarantee in favour of a creditor of the corporate debtor where that guarantee has been invoked and remains unpaid. Section 240A switches off clauses (c) and (h) alone where the corporate debtor is a micro, small or medium enterprise, so a promoter of an MSME may bid for his own company — but every other clause of section 29A, including clause (b) on an undischarged insolvent and clause (d) on a conviction, applies to him unchanged.

concepts.subsection: Pre-packaged insolvency resolution process — Chapter III-A of the IBC
concepts.statement: Chapter III-A, sections 54A to 54P, opens the pre-packaged insolvency resolution process to one class of debtor only — a corporate debtor classified as a micro, small or medium enterprise under section 7(1) of the MSMED Act, 2006. The minimum default is ten lakh rupees, notified under the second proviso to section 4 by S.O. 1543(E) dated 9 April 2021, against the one crore rupees that gates an ordinary corporate insolvency resolution process. Before filing, the corporate debtor must obtain the approval of unrelated financial creditors representing not less than sixty-six per cent in value of the financial debt owed to them, and must place a base resolution plan on the table. The whole process is built to close within one hundred and twenty days, against the outer three hundred and thirty of a full process, and management stays with the existing board — a debtor-in-possession process supervised by a resolution professional, not an ouster of the board.

citation.ref: Sections 54A and 54C of Chapter III-A, read with the second proviso to section 4 and notification S.O. 1543(E) dated 9 April 2021

concepts.subsection: FDI receipt — the Companies Act clock and the FEMA clock
concepts.statement: A single foreign investment starts two clocks with two regulators. Under company law, section 42(6) requires allotment within sixty days of receipt of the application money, refund within fifteen days of that period if allotment does not happen, and interest at twelve per cent beyond that; section 42(8) then requires the return of allotment with the Registrar within fifteen days of the allotment, and section 42(4) blocks the company from using the money until it is filed. Under FEMA, Regulation 4(1) of the Foreign Exchange Management (Mode of Payment and Reporting of Non-Debt Instruments) Regulations, 2019 requires the issue to be reported to the Reserve Bank in Form FC-GPR not later than thirty days from the date of issue of the equity instruments, and Regulation 5 makes a late filing payable through a late submission fee. The two filings run from the same allotment, to different authorities, on different lengths of leash — filing one never satisfies the other.

citation.ref: Regulations 4(1) and 5 of the FEM (Mode of Payment and Reporting of Non-Debt Instruments) Regulations, 2019, read with sections 42(4), 42(6) and 42(8) of the Companies Act, 2013

concepts.subsection: Overseas direct investment against overseas portfolio investment
concepts.statement: Rule 2(1)(q) of the FEM (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022 makes an investment overseas direct investment where it is an acquisition of unlisted equity capital of a foreign entity, or a subscription to its memorandum, or an acquisition of ten per cent or more of the paid-up equity capital of a listed foreign entity, or any investment below ten per cent that carries control. Rule 2(1)(s) leaves everything else in foreign securities as overseas portfolio investment. The Explanation to Rule 2(1)(q) is the sting — once an investment is classified as ODI it stays ODI even if the holding later falls below ten per cent or control is lost, so the reporting and exit discipline follows the original classification, not today's percentage. Paragraph 3(1) of Schedule I caps an Indian entity's total financial commitment in all foreign entities at four hundred per cent of its net worth as per the last audited balance sheet, Rule 19(1) bars ODI into real estate activity, gambling and rupee-linked financial products without approval, and reporting, including the Annual Performance Report, runs through Regulation 10 of the FEM (Overseas Investment) Regulations, 2022.

citation.ref: Rules 2(1)(q) with its Explanation, 2(1)(s) and 19(1), and paragraph 3(1) of Schedule I, of the FEM (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022, read with Regulation 10 of the FEM (Overseas Investment) Regulations, 2022

concepts.subsection: Compounding a FEMA contravention — section 15 and the 2024 Rules
concepts.statement: A contravention of FEMA carries a penalty under section 13, and section 15 lets the contravener compound it — admit it, pay a sum, and close the matter — on an application made after the contravention. The Foreign Exchange (Compounding Proceedings) Rules, 2024, notified on 12 September 2024, superseded the 2000 Rules and moved every figure: the application fee is now ten thousand rupees plus tax, and the Reserve Bank officer who may compound is fixed by the amount involved — an Assistant General Manager below sixty lakh rupees, a Deputy General Manager below two crore fifty lakh rupees, a General Manager below five crore rupees, and a Chief General Manager above five crore rupees. The compounding order is to be passed within one hundred and eighty days of receipt of a complete application, and the amount is payable within fifteen days of the order, failing which the application is void and FEMA applies to the contravention as though nothing had happened. A contravention of clause (a) of section 3 — dealing in foreign exchange with an unauthorised person — is not compounded by the Reserve Bank at all; it goes to the Directorate of Enforcement.

citation.ref: Sections 13 and 15, read with the Foreign Exchange (Compounding Proceedings) Rules, 2024 (notified 12 September 2024)

concepts.subsection: Insider trading — continual disclosure and the contra trade bar
concepts.statement: Regulation 7(2)(a) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 makes every promoter, member of the promoter group, designated person and director disclose to the company the securities acquired or disposed of, within two trading days, once the value traded — in one transaction or a series over any calendar quarter — exceeds ten lakh rupees. Regulation 7(2)(b) then makes the company notify the stock exchange within two trading days of receiving that disclosure. Separately, clause 10 of Schedule B to Regulation 9 makes the company's code of conduct forbid a designated person who has traded from executing a contra trade for a period that can never be shorter than six months; a contra trade done in breach has its profits disgorged to SEBI for credit to the Investor Protection and Education Fund. The compliance officer may relax the restriction for reasons recorded in writing, but a relaxation can never permit what the Regulations themselves prohibit.

citation.ref: Regulations 7(2)(a) and 7(2)(b), and clause 10 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9

concepts.subsection: Substantial acquisition — when an open offer is triggered
